powfacpy.applications.dynamic_modal_analysis

Dynamic modal (small-signal) analysis.

Wraps PowerFactory's modal analysis command (ComMod) to compute, for whatever state is currently active (activate the study case/scenario/ operating point yourself first, as with DynamicSimulation or StaticCalc):

  • the system's eigenvalues, their damping ratio, natural and damped frequency, and dominant states (ModalAnalysis, ModalAnalysisResults);
  • participation factors of each state in each eigenvalue (ParticipationFactorSet);
  • how the eigenvalues move as a parameter changes and the sensitivity of an eigenvalue's metrics to that change (track_eigenvalues, EigenvalueSweepResults, Sensitivity, sensitivity_between, ParametricSensitivity) - built on top of parstudy.Study (see the Parameter Studies tutorial) rather than a bespoke sweep loop: evaluate() calls ModalAnalysis.run() once per point, parstudy handles the sweep strategy and snapshot/restore, and the helpers here turn the resulting sequence of ModalAnalysisResults into a consistently-indexed eigenvalue trajectory (PowerFactory does not guarantee eigenvalues come back in the same order run to run);
  • two ways to get an eigenvalue's sensitivity to a parameter: sensitivity_between finite-differences the eigenvalues between two (tracked) runs; the analytical, eigenvector-weighted ModalAnalysisResults.eigenvalue_sensitivity needs only dA/dp (usually itself a finite difference of the state matrix - system_matrix_sensitivity) evaluated at a single run, so it needs no eigenvalue tracking at all. See the tutorial for a comparison of both on the same system.

See the Dynamic Modal Analysis tutorial, which also shows the connection to powfacpy.applications.dynamic_simulation: a poorly-damped or unstable mode found here should be visible as a sustained or growing oscillation in a time-domain simulation of the same parameter point.

Needs the optional 'scipy' dependency: pip install powfacpy[dynamic_modal_analysis]. Eigenvalue sweeps additionally need 'parstudy': pip install powfacpy[parstudy].

   1"""Dynamic modal (small-signal) analysis.
   2
   3Wraps PowerFactory's modal analysis command (`ComMod`) to compute, for
   4whatever state is currently active (activate the study case/scenario/
   5operating point yourself first, as with `DynamicSimulation` or `StaticCalc`):
   6
   7- the system's eigenvalues, their damping ratio, natural and damped
   8  frequency, and dominant states (`ModalAnalysis`, `ModalAnalysisResults`);
   9- participation factors of each state in each eigenvalue
  10  (`ParticipationFactorSet`);
  11- how the eigenvalues move as a parameter changes and the sensitivity of an
  12  eigenvalue's metrics to that change (`track_eigenvalues`,
  13  `EigenvalueSweepResults`, `Sensitivity`, `sensitivity_between`,
  14  `ParametricSensitivity`) - built on top of `parstudy.Study` (see the
  15  *Parameter Studies* tutorial) rather than a bespoke sweep loop: `evaluate()`
  16  calls `ModalAnalysis.run()` once per point, `parstudy` handles the sweep
  17  strategy and snapshot/restore, and the helpers here turn the resulting
  18  sequence of `ModalAnalysisResults` into a consistently-indexed eigenvalue
  19  trajectory (PowerFactory does not guarantee eigenvalues come back in the
  20  same order run to run);
  21- two ways to get an eigenvalue's sensitivity to a parameter: `sensitivity_between`
  22  finite-differences the *eigenvalues* between two (tracked) runs; the
  23  analytical, eigenvector-weighted `ModalAnalysisResults.eigenvalue_sensitivity`
  24  needs only `dA/dp` (usually itself a finite difference of the *state
  25  matrix* - `system_matrix_sensitivity`) evaluated at a single run, so it
  26  needs no eigenvalue tracking at all. See the tutorial for a comparison of
  27  both on the same system.
  28
  29See the *Dynamic Modal Analysis* tutorial, which also shows the connection to
  30`powfacpy.applications.dynamic_simulation`: a poorly-damped or unstable mode
  31found here should be visible as a sustained or growing oscillation in a
  32time-domain simulation of the same parameter point.
  33
  34Needs the optional 'scipy' dependency: `pip install powfacpy[dynamic_modal_analysis]`.
  35Eigenvalue *sweeps* additionally need 'parstudy': `pip install powfacpy[parstudy]`.
  36"""

  73# Column names shared by the eigenvalue / participation-factor / modal-results
  74# DataFrames.
  75INDEX_COL = "Index"
  76REAL_COL = "Real (1/s)"
  77IMAG_COL = "Imag (rad/s)"
  78NATURAL_FREQ_COL = "Undamped natural frequency (Hz)"
  79DAMPED_FREQ_COL = "Damped frequency (Hz)"
  80DAMPING_RATIO_COL = "Damping ratio"
  81MODE_COL = "Mode"
  82DOMINANT_STATES_COL = "Dominant states"
  83
  84_STYLE_PRECISION = 4
  85#: default quantile (of the real part) used by the eigenvalue-plotting
  86#: methods' `xlim="auto"` to zoom in on the dominant (slowest-decaying, least
  87#: negative) eigenvalues instead of letting a handful of very fast/heavily
  88#: damped ones stretch the x-axis.
  89DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE = 0.75
  90
  91
  92def _auto_real_xlim(
  93    real_parts: npt.NDArray, quantile: float = DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE
  94) -> tuple[float, float]:
  95    """A `(lo, hi)` x-axis range framing the dominant eigenvalues - those
  96    with the largest (least negative) real part, which decay slowest and
  97    therefore dominate the long-term time response - instead of the full
  98    range, which a handful of very fast/heavily-damped eigenvalues can
  99    otherwise stretch until the dominant ones are an unreadable cluster near
 100    the origin.
 101
 102    `lo` is the `quantile`-th percentile of the real parts (raise `quantile`
 103    to zoom in further, lower it to include more of the faster eigenvalues);
 104    `hi` is just past the largest real part (at least 0, so the
 105    stable/unstable boundary is always visible).
 106    """
 107    real_parts = np.asarray(real_parts, dtype=float)
 108    hi = max(float(np.max(real_parts)), 0.0)
 109    lo = min(float(np.quantile(real_parts, quantile)), hi - 1.0)
 110    lo = max(lo, float(np.min(real_parts)))
 111    span = hi - lo
 112    margin = 0.15 * span if span > 0 else 1.0
 113    return lo - margin, hi + margin

 121class Eigenvalue:
 122    """A single eigenvalue of the system state matrix, with the natural
 123    frequency, damped frequency and damping ratio derived from it. Immutable.
 124    """
 125
 126    EPSILON = 1e-9
 127    "Imaginary part below which an eigenvalue is treated as purely real."
 128
 129    def __init__(self, value: complex | float, index: int) -> None:
 130        """
 131        Args:
 132            value: the eigenvalue's real and/or imaginary part.
 133            index: the eigenvalue's index (1-based, matching PowerFactory's
 134                own numbering of the state matrix).
 135        """
 136        self.index = index
 137        self.value = complex(value)
 138        self.nat_freq = self._natural_frequency(self.value)
 139        self.damp_freq = self._damped_frequency(self.value)
 140        self.damp_ratio = self._damping_ratio(self.value)
 141
 142    def get_index(self) -> int:
 143        return self.index
 144
 145    def get_value(self) -> complex:
 146        return self.value
 147
 148    def get_imag(self) -> float:
 149        return self.value.imag
 150
 151    def get_nat_freq(self) -> float:
 152        return self.nat_freq
 153
 154    def get_damp_ratio(self) -> float:
 155        return self.damp_ratio
 156
 157    def get_series(self) -> Series:
 158        """A `Series` with this eigenvalue and the quantities derived from it."""
 159        return pd.Series(
 160            {
 161                INDEX_COL: self.index,
 162                REAL_COL: self.value.real,
 163                IMAG_COL: self.value.imag,
 164                NATURAL_FREQ_COL: self.nat_freq,
 165                DAMPED_FREQ_COL: self.damp_freq,
 166                DAMPING_RATIO_COL: self.damp_ratio,
 167            }
 168        )
 169
 170    def set_index(self, index: int) -> Self:
 171        """A copy of this eigenvalue with a different index (does not mutate `self`)."""
 172        return Eigenvalue(self.value, index)
 173
 174    def _damping_ratio(self, eig: complex) -> float:
 175        if abs(eig.real) < self.EPSILON and abs(eig.imag) < self.EPSILON:
 176            return 1.0
 177        return -eig.real / math.sqrt(eig.real**2 + eig.imag**2)
 178
 179    def _natural_frequency(self, eig: complex) -> float:
 180        if abs(eig.imag) < self.EPSILON:
 181            return 0.0
 182        w_n = math.sqrt(eig.real**2 + eig.imag**2)
 183        return w_n / (2 * math.pi)
 184
 185    def _damped_frequency(self, eig: complex) -> float:
 186        w_n = 2 * math.pi * self._natural_frequency(eig)
 187        zeta = self._damping_ratio(eig)
 188        w_d = w_n * math.sqrt(max(1 - zeta**2, 0.0))
 189        return w_d / (2 * math.pi)
 190
 191    def __lt__(self, other: Self) -> bool:
 192        return self.index < other.index
 193
 194    def __copy__(self) -> Self:
 195        return Eigenvalue(self.value, self.index)
 196
 197    def __repr__(self) -> str:
 198        return f"Eigenvalue({self.value.real:.4f}{self.value.imag:+.4f}j, index={self.index})"
 199

 201class EigenvalueSet:
 202    """An immutable set of `Eigenvalue`s, e.g. all the eigenvalues of one
 203    modal analysis run."""
 204
 205    def __init__(
 206        self,
 207        eigenvalues: npt.NDArray | list[Eigenvalue],
 208        indexes: int | list[int] | None = None,
 209    ) -> None:
 210        """
 211        Args:
 212            eigenvalues: an array of eigenvalues, or a list of `Eigenvalue` objects.
 213            indexes: a single index or list of indexes for the eigenvalues.
 214                If `eigenvalues` is an array and `indexes` is omitted, they
 215                are indexed 1..len(eigenvalues). If a list of `Eigenvalue`
 216                objects is passed together with `indexes`, they are reindexed.
 217        """
 218        indexes = self._handle_indexes(indexes, eigenvalues)
 219        if isinstance(eigenvalues, np.ndarray):
 220            self.eigenvalues = self._from_array(eigenvalues, indexes)
 221        else:
 222            self.eigenvalues = self._from_list(eigenvalues, indexes)
 223        self.df = self._create_dataframe(self.eigenvalues)
 224        self._iter_pos = 0
 225
 226    def get_indexes(self) -> list[int]:
 227        return [e.get_index() for e in self.eigenvalues]
 228
 229    def get_vector(self) -> npt.NDArray:
 230        """The eigenvalues as a complex vector, in index order."""
 231        real = self.df[REAL_COL].to_numpy()
 232        imag = self.df[IMAG_COL].to_numpy()
 233        return real + 1j * imag
 234
 235    def get_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
 236        """One row per eigenvalue: real/imaginary part, natural/damped
 237        frequency and damping ratio, indexed by eigenvalue index."""
 238        return self.df.copy()
 239
 240    def filter_by_index(self, indexes: int | list[int]) -> Self:
 241        """Keep only the eigenvalues at the given index(es)."""
 242        indexes = self._normalize_indexes(indexes)
 243        eigenvalues = [e for e in self.eigenvalues if e.get_index() in indexes]
 244        return EigenvalueSet(eigenvalues)
 245
 246    def filter_by_damping_ratio(self, max_damping_ratio: float) -> Self:
 247        """Drop eigenvalues whose damping ratio is above `max_damping_ratio`
 248        - i.e. keep the poorly-damped/unstable ones."""
 249        eigenvalues = [
 250            e for e in self.eigenvalues if e.get_damp_ratio() <= max_damping_ratio
 251        ]
 252        return EigenvalueSet(eigenvalues)
 253
 254    def filter_out_conjugates(self) -> Self:
 255        """Keep only one eigenvalue of each complex-conjugate pair (the one
 256        with non-negative imaginary part)."""
 257        eigenvalues = [e for e in self.eigenvalues if e.get_imag() >= 0]
 258        return EigenvalueSet(eigenvalues)
 259
 260    def filter_out_real_modes(self) -> Self:
 261        """Keep only the complex (oscillatory) eigenvalues."""
 262        eigenvalues = [
 263            e for e in self.eigenvalues if abs(e.get_imag()) >= Eigenvalue.EPSILON
 264        ]
 265        return EigenvalueSet(eigenvalues)
 266
 267    def map_eigenvalues(self, index_map: dict[int, int]) -> Self:
 268        """Reindex the eigenvalues according to a map from current to new index."""
 269        eigenvalues = [e.set_index(index_map[e.get_index()]) for e in self.eigenvalues]
 270        return EigenvalueSet(eigenvalues)
 271
 272    def plot(
 273        self,
 274        ax: plt.Axes | None = None,
 275        *,
 276        xlim: tuple[float, float] | Literal["auto"] | None = "auto",
 277        quantile: float = DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE,
 278    ) -> plt.Axes:
 279        """Scatter the eigenvalues in the complex plane, shading the unstable
 280        (right) half-plane.
 281
 282        Args:
 283            ax: axes to draw on (a new figure is created if omitted).
 284            xlim: `"auto"` (default) zooms the x-axis to the dominant
 285                eigenvalues via `_auto_real_xlim`; pass an explicit `(lo, hi)`
 286                to override, or `None` for matplotlib's own full-range default.
 287            quantile: only used when `xlim="auto"`. The fraction of
 288                eigenvalues (by real part) to zoom *out* past - e.g. the
 289                default 0.75 frames roughly the most dominant quarter of
 290                eigenvalues; raise it (closer to 1) to zoom in on fewer,
 291                more dominant eigenvalues, or lower it to include more of
 292                the faster/better-damped ones.
 293        """
 294        if ax is None:
 295            _, ax = plt.subplots()
 296        df = self.get_dataframe()
 297        ax.scatter(df[REAL_COL], df[IMAG_COL], marker="x")
 298        if xlim == "auto":
 299            xlim = _auto_real_xlim(df[REAL_COL].to_numpy(), quantile=quantile)
 300        if xlim is not None:
 301            ax.set_xlim(xlim)
 302        left, right = ax.get_xlim()
 303        ax.axvspan(0, right, facecolor="red", alpha=0.2)
 304        ax.set_xlim([left, right])
 305        ax.set_xlabel("Real")
 306        ax.set_ylabel("Imaginary")
 307        ax.set_title("Eigenvalues")
 308        ax.grid(True)
 309        return ax
 310
 311    def _create_dataframe(self, eigenvalues: list[Eigenvalue]) -> DataFrame:
 312        return (
 313            pd.concat([e.get_series() for e in eigenvalues], axis=1)
 314            .T.astype({INDEX_COL: int})
 315            .set_index(INDEX_COL)
 316        )
 317
 318    def _handle_indexes(
 319        self,
 320        indexes: int | list[int] | None,
 321        eigenvalues: npt.NDArray | list[Eigenvalue],
 322    ) -> list[int] | None:
 323        if indexes is None:
 324            if isinstance(eigenvalues, np.ndarray):
 325                return list(range(1, len(eigenvalues) + 1))
 326            return None
 327        return self._normalize_indexes(indexes)
 328
 329    def _normalize_indexes(self, indexes: int | list[int]) -> list[int]:
 330        return [indexes] if isinstance(indexes, (int, np.integer)) else list(indexes)
 331
 332    def _from_array(
 333        self, array: npt.NDArray, indexes: list[int]
 334    ) -> list[Eigenvalue]:
 335        eigenvalues = [Eigenvalue(value, idx) for value, idx in zip(array, indexes)]
 336        eigenvalues.sort()
 337        return eigenvalues
 338
 339    def _from_list(
 340        self, eigenvalues: list[Eigenvalue], indexes: list[int] | None
 341    ) -> list[Eigenvalue]:
 342        if indexes:
 343            eigenvalues = [e.set_index(idx) for e, idx in zip(eigenvalues, indexes)]
 344        eigenvalues = list(eigenvalues)
 345        eigenvalues.sort()
 346        return eigenvalues
 347
 348    def __sub__(self, other: Self) -> DataFrame:
 349        """Difference of the two sets, column by column (real/imag part,
 350        frequencies, damping ratio), row-aligned by eigenvalue index -
 351        track_eigenvalues()/track_eigenvalues_from() first if the indexes
 352        might not already correspond to the same physical mode."""
 353        self_df, other_df = self.get_dataframe(), other.get_dataframe()
 354        if len(self_df.index) != len(other_df.index):
 355            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
 356                "Cannot subtract eigenvalue sets of different length: "
 357                f"{len(self_df.index)} vs {len(other_df.index)}."
 358            )
 359        return self_df - other_df
 360
 361    def __len__(self) -> int:
 362        return len(self.eigenvalues)
 363
 364    def __iter__(self) -> Self:
 365        self._iter_pos = 0
 366        return self
 367
 368    def __next__(self) -> Eigenvalue:
 369        if self._iter_pos >= len(self):
 370            raise StopIteration
 371        e = self.eigenvalues[self._iter_pos]
 372        self._iter_pos += 1
 373        return e
 374
 375    def __repr__(self) -> str:
 376        return f"EigenvalueSet({np.array2string(self.get_vector(), precision=2, suppress_small=True)})"
 377

 379class ParticipationFactor:
 380    """The participation of every state in a single eigenvalue."""
 381
 382    def __init__(
 383        self, participation: npt.NDArray, states: npt.NDArray[np.str_], index: int
 384    ) -> None:
 385        if participation.ndim > 1 or states.ndim > 1:
 386            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
 387                "'participation' and 'states' must both be one-dimensional; got "
 388                f"{participation.ndim} and {states.ndim} dimensions."
 389            )
 390        self.participation = participation
 391        self.states = states
 392        self.index = index
 393
 394    def get_index(self) -> int:
 395        return self.index
 396
 397    def get_array(self) -> npt.NDArray:
 398        return self.participation
 399
 400    def get_series(self) -> Series:
 401        # Built from plain lists (not np.insert into self.states) because a
 402        # fixed-width numpy string array (e.g. dtype '<U1' for single-char
 403        # state names) would silently truncate the "Index" label.
 404        index = [INDEX_COL, *self.states.tolist()]
 405        values = [self.index, *self.participation.tolist()]
 406        return pd.Series(values, index=index)
 407
 408    def set_index(self, index: int) -> Self:
 409        """A copy with a different eigenvalue index (does not mutate `self`)."""
 410        return ParticipationFactor(self.participation, self.states, index)
 411
 412    def filter_by_states(self, states: str | list[str]) -> Self:
 413        states_to_keep = {states} if isinstance(states, str) else set(states)
 414        mask = np.isin(self.states, list(states_to_keep))
 415        return ParticipationFactor(self.participation[mask], self.states[mask], self.index)
 416
 417    def __lt__(self, other: Self) -> bool:
 418        return self.index < other.index
 419

 421class ParticipationFactorSet:
 422    """Participation factors of every state in every eigenvalue of one modal
 423    analysis run - a `(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix."""
 424
 425    def __init__(
 426        self,
 427        participations: npt.NDArray | list[ParticipationFactor],
 428        states: npt.NDArray[np.str_] | None = None,
 429        indexes: int | list[int] | None = None,
 430    ) -> None:
 431        """
 432        Args:
 433            participations: a `(state, eigenvalue)` array, or a list of
 434                `ParticipationFactor` objects (one per eigenvalue).
 435            states: state names - required when `participations` is an array.
 436            indexes: eigenvalue indexes (one per column of `participations`).
 437                Defaults to 1..n.
 438        """
 439        indexes = self._handle_indexes(indexes, participations)
 440        if isinstance(participations, np.ndarray):
 441            if states is None:
 442                raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
 443                    "'states' must be given when 'participations' is an array."
 444                )
 445            self.parts = [
 446                ParticipationFactor(participations[:, n], states, idx)
 447                for n, idx in enumerate(indexes)
 448            ]
 449            self.parts.sort()
 450        else:
 451            parts = list(participations)
 452            if indexes:
 453                parts = [p.set_index(idx) for p, idx in zip(parts, indexes)]
 454            parts.sort()
 455            self.parts = parts
 456        self.df = self._create_dataframe(self.parts)
 457        self._iter_pos = 0
 458
 459    def get_states(self) -> npt.NDArray[np.str_]:
 460        return self.df.index.to_numpy()
 461
 462    def get_array(self) -> npt.NDArray:
 463        return self.df.to_numpy()
 464
 465    def get_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
 466        """`(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix of participation factors."""
 467        return self.df.copy()
 468
 469    def filter_by_eigenvalue_index(self, index: int | list[int]) -> Self:
 470        indexes = self._normalize_indexes(index)
 471        parts = [p for p in self.parts if p.get_index() in indexes]
 472        return ParticipationFactorSet(parts)
 473
 474    def filter_by_states(self, states: str | list[str]) -> Self:
 475        parts = [p.filter_by_states(states) for p in self.parts]
 476        return ParticipationFactorSet(parts)
 477
 478    def filter_by_min_state_participation(self, min_participation: float) -> Self:
 479        """Keep only states whose participation, summed over every eigenvalue
 480        currently in this set, is at least `min_participation`."""
 481        totals = self.df.sum(axis=1)
 482        states_to_keep = totals.index[totals >= min_participation].tolist()
 483        return self.filter_by_states(states_to_keep)
 484
 485    def map_eigenvalues(self, index_map: dict[int, int]) -> Self:
 486        parts = [p.set_index(index_map[p.get_index()]) for p in self.parts]
 487        return ParticipationFactorSet(parts)
 488
 489    def plot(self, *, top_n: int | None = 15) -> plt.Figure:
 490        """Horizontal bar chart of the participation of every state - one
 491        panel per eigenvalue currently in this set.
 492
 493        Args:
 494            top_n: only the `top_n` states with the highest total
 495                participation (summed over every eigenvalue currently in
 496                this set) are shown - with many states, showing all of them
 497                makes the y-axis labels unreadably crowded. `None` shows
 498                every state.
 499        """
 500        df = self.get_dataframe()
 501        if top_n is not None and len(df.index) > top_n:
 502            top_states = df.sum(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False).index[:top_n]
 503            df = df.loc[top_states]
 504        states = df.index.tolist()
 505        y_pos = np.arange(len(states))
 506        eigenvalue_indexes = df.columns.tolist()
 507        fig, axes = plt.subplots(
 508            len(eigenvalue_indexes),
 509            1,
 510            squeeze=False,
 511            figsize=(6, 0.3 * len(states) + 1.2 * len(eigenvalue_indexes)),
 512        )
 513        for row, idx in enumerate(eigenvalue_indexes):
 514            ax = axes[row][0]
 515            ax.barh(y_pos, df[idx].to_numpy())
 516            ax.set_yticks(y_pos, labels=states, fontsize="small")
 517            ax.set_xlabel("Participation")
 518            ax.set_title(f"Eigenvalue {idx}")
 519        fig.tight_layout()
 520        return fig
 521
 522    def _create_dataframe(self, parts: list[ParticipationFactor]) -> DataFrame:
 523        return (
 524            pd.concat([p.get_series() for p in parts], axis=1)
 525            .T.astype({INDEX_COL: int})
 526            .set_index(INDEX_COL)
 527            .T
 528        )
 529
 530    def _handle_indexes(
 531        self,
 532        indexes: int | list[int] | None,
 533        participations: npt.NDArray | list[ParticipationFactor],
 534    ) -> list[int] | None:
 535        if indexes is None:
 536            if isinstance(participations, np.ndarray):
 537                return list(range(1, participations.shape[1] + 1))
 538            return None
 539        return self._normalize_indexes(indexes)
 540
 541    def _normalize_indexes(self, indexes: int | list[int]) -> list[int]:
 542        return [indexes] if isinstance(indexes, (int, np.integer)) else list(indexes)
 543
 544    def __len__(self) -> int:
 545        return len(self.parts)
 546
 547    def __iter__(self) -> Self:
 548        self._iter_pos = 0
 549        return self
 550
 551    def __next__(self) -> ParticipationFactor:
 552        if self._iter_pos >= len(self):
 553            raise StopIteration
 554        p = self.parts[self._iter_pos]
 555        self._iter_pos += 1
 556        return p
 557

 559# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
 560# eigenvalue tracking
 561# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
 562
 563
 564class _IndexCandidate:
 565    """One candidate mapping from a scrambled eigenvalue's current position to
 566    a reference eigenvalue's position, with a certainty score (higher = better)."""
 567
 568    def __init__(self, current_position: int, target_position: int, certainty: float) -> None:
 569        self.current_position = current_position
 570        self.target_position = target_position
 571        self.certainty = certainty
 572
 573
 574class _EigenvaluePositionElection:
 575    """Assigns each scrambled eigenvalue position a unique target position by
 576    repeatedly picking the remaining candidate pair with the highest certainty."""
 577
 578    def __init__(self, current_indexes: list[int], target_indexes: list[int]) -> None:
 579        self.candidates: dict[int, dict[int, _IndexCandidate | None]] = {
 580            n: {m: None for m in target_indexes} for n in current_indexes
 581        }
 582        self.winners: dict[int, int] = {n: -1 for n in current_indexes}
 583
 584    def add_candidates(self, candidates: list[_IndexCandidate]) -> None:
 585        for candidate in candidates:
 586            existing = self.candidates[candidate.current_position].get(
 587                candidate.target_position
 588            )
 589            if existing is not None:
 590                candidate = _IndexCandidate(
 591                    candidate.current_position,
 592                    candidate.target_position,
 593                    existing.certainty + candidate.certainty,
 594                )
 595            self.candidates[candidate.current_position][candidate.target_position] = (
 596                candidate
 597            )
 598
 599    def elect_best_candidate(self) -> bool:
 600        """Elect the remaining candidate with the highest certainty. Returns
 601        False (without electing anything) once no candidates remain."""
 602        best: _IndexCandidate | None = None
 603        for candidates in self.candidates.values():
 604            for candidate in candidates.values():
 605                if candidate is not None and (
 606                    best is None or candidate.certainty > best.certainty
 607                ):
 608                    best = candidate
 609        if best is None:
 610            return False
 611
 612        self.winners[best.current_position] = best.target_position
 613        for target in self.candidates[best.current_position]:
 614            self.candidates[best.current_position][target] = None
 615        for candidates in self.candidates.values():
 616            candidates[best.target_position] = None
 617        return True
 618
 619    def get_winners(self) -> dict[int, int]:
 620        return self.winners
 621
 622
 623class EigenvalueTracker:
 624    """Reorders a 'scrambled' set of eigenvalues (and matching participation
 625    factors) to line up index-for-index with a reference set from another
 626    run - PowerFactory does not guarantee eigenvalues come back in the same
 627    order between two modal analyses.
 628
 629    Candidates for "this scrambled eigenvalue is that reference eigenvalue"
 630    are scored by three independent distances (nearest eigenvalue in the
 631    complex plane, nearest participation-factor vector, nearest natural
 632    frequency - the latter weighted up, since it discriminates well between
 633    otherwise-similar complex-conjugate-like pairs) and elected by taking the
 634    best-scoring pair first, repeatedly, until every position is assigned.
 635    """
 636
 637    #: weight amplifying the natural-frequency distance relative to the
 638    #: eigenvalue and participation-factor distances (chosen empirically).
 639    NATURAL_FREQUENCY_WEIGHT = 3
 640    #: the maximum possible distance between two (normalized) participation vectors.
 641    PARTICIPATION_NORMALIZATION = 2
 642
 643    def __init__(
 644        self,
 645        eig_ref: EigenvalueSet,
 646        eig_scrambled: EigenvalueSet,
 647        pf_ref: ParticipationFactorSet,
 648        pf_scrambled: ParticipationFactorSet,
 649    ) -> None:
 650        """
 651        Args:
 652            eig_ref: eigenvalues of the reference run.
 653            eig_scrambled: eigenvalues to reorder to match `eig_ref`.
 654            pf_ref: participation factors of the reference run.
 655            pf_scrambled: participation factors matching `eig_scrambled`.
 656        """
 657        if len(eig_ref) != len(eig_scrambled):
 658            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
 659                f"Length of eigenvalue sets must match to track them: got "
 660                f"{len(eig_ref)} and {len(eig_scrambled)}."
 661            )
 662        self.eig_ref = eig_ref
 663        self.eig_scrambled = eig_scrambled
 664        self.pf_ref = pf_ref
 665        self.pf_scrambled = pf_scrambled
 666        self.election = _EigenvaluePositionElection(
 667            eig_scrambled.get_indexes(), eig_ref.get_indexes()
 668        )
 669
 670    def calculate_index_map(self) -> dict[int, int]:
 671        """Compute the map from `eig_scrambled`'s current indexes to the
 672        index of the reference eigenvalue each one is deemed to correspond to."""
 673        self._add_eigenvalue_distance_candidates()
 674        self._add_participation_distance_candidates()
 675        self._add_natural_frequency_distance_candidates()
 676        while self.election.elect_best_candidate():
 677            pass
 678        index_map = self.election.get_winners()
 679
 680        if len(set(index_map.values())) < len(index_map):
 681            raise PFEigenvalueTrackingError(
 682                "Eigenvalue tracking is ambiguous: two or more eigenvalues "
 683                "would map to the same position.\n"
 684                f"Reference eigenvalues: {self.eig_ref!r}\n"
 685                f"Scrambled eigenvalues: {self.eig_scrambled!r}\n"
 686                f"Index map: {index_map}"
 687            )
 688        return index_map
 689
 690    def unscramble(self) -> tuple[EigenvalueSet, ParticipationFactorSet]:
 691        """Reorder `eig_scrambled` / `pf_scrambled` to match `eig_ref`'s order."""
 692        index_map = self.calculate_index_map()
 693        return (
 694            self.eig_scrambled.map_eigenvalues(index_map),
 695            self.pf_scrambled.map_eigenvalues(index_map),
 696        )
 697
 698    def _add_eigenvalue_distance_candidates(self) -> None:
 699        for eig in self.eig_scrambled:
 700            candidates = [
 701                _IndexCandidate(
 702                    eig.get_index(),
 703                    ref.get_index(),
 704                    -abs(ref.get_value() - eig.get_value()),
 705                )
 706                for ref in self.eig_ref
 707            ]
 708            self.election.add_candidates(candidates)
 709
 710    def _add_participation_distance_candidates(self) -> None:
 711        for pf in self.pf_scrambled:
 712            candidates = [
 713                _IndexCandidate(
 714                    pf.get_index(),
 715                    ref.get_index(),
 716                    -np.linalg.norm(ref.get_array() - pf.get_array())
 717                    / self.PARTICIPATION_NORMALIZATION,
 718                )
 719                for ref in self.pf_ref
 720            ]
 721            self.election.add_candidates(candidates)
 722
 723    def _add_natural_frequency_distance_candidates(self) -> None:
 724        for eig in self.eig_scrambled:
 725            candidates = [
 726                _IndexCandidate(
 727                    eig.get_index(),
 728                    ref.get_index(),
 729                    -abs(ref.get_nat_freq() - eig.get_nat_freq())
 730                    * self.NATURAL_FREQUENCY_WEIGHT,
 731                )
 732                for ref in self.eig_ref
 733            ]
 734            self.election.add_candidates(candidates)
 735
 736
 737def track_eigenvalues(results: Sequence["ModalAnalysisResults"]) -> list["ModalAnalysisResults"]:
 738    """Track eigenvalues across a sequence of modal analysis runs (e.g. the
 739    `raw` results of a `parstudy.Study` sweep), so every result's eigenvalue
 740    index consistently refers to the same physical mode.
 741
 742    Each result is tracked against the *previous* (already-tracked) one, not
 743    against the first, so a mode can drift gradually across many runs without
 744    ever being compared to a very different reference.
 745
 746    Args:
 747        results: the modal analysis results in run order. The first is kept
 748            as-is and used as the initial reference.
 749
 750    Returns:
 751        A new list of `ModalAnalysisResults`, reindexed to be consistent
 752        with one another.
 753    """
 754    tracked: list[ModalAnalysisResults] = []
 755    for i, result in enumerate(results):
 756        if i == 0:
 757            tracked.append(result)
 758        else:
 759            tracked.append(result.track_eigenvalues_from(tracked[-1]))
 760    return tracked
 761

 763# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
 764# modal analysis
 765# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
 766
 767
 768class ModalAnalysisResults:
 769    """Result of one modal analysis run: eigenvalues, participation factors
 770    and the system (state) matrix they were computed from."""
 771
 772    #: minimum participation for a state to be listed as "dominant" for a mode.
 773    DOMINANT_STATES_MIN_PARTICIPATION = 0.05
 774
 775    def __init__(
 776        self,
 777        sys_matrix: npt.NDArray[np.complex128],
 778        eigenvalues: EigenvalueSet,
 779        participation_factors: ParticipationFactorSet,
 780        *,
 781        right_eigenvectors: DataFrame | None = None,
 782        left_eigenvectors: DataFrame | None = None,
 783    ) -> None:
 784        """
 785        Args:
 786            sys_matrix: the system (state) matrix.
 787            eigenvalues: the eigenvalues.
 788            participation_factors: participation of every state in every eigenvalue.
 789            right_eigenvectors: `(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix of the raw
 790                (complex, unnormalized) right eigenvectors - needed for
 791                `eigenvalue_sensitivity`. `None` if not computed (e.g. a
 792                `ModalAnalysisResults` built by hand without them).
 793            left_eigenvectors: the matching left eigenvectors.
 794        """
 795        self.sys_matrix = sys_matrix
 796        self.eigenvalues = eigenvalues
 797        self.participation_factors = participation_factors
 798        self.right_eigenvectors = right_eigenvectors
 799        self.left_eigenvectors = left_eigenvectors
 800
 801    def filter_by_damping_ratio(self, max_damping_ratio: float) -> Self:
 802        """Keep only the eigenvalues with a damping ratio at or below
 803        `max_damping_ratio` - i.e. the poorly-damped/unstable ones."""
 804        eigenvalues = self.eigenvalues.filter_by_damping_ratio(max_damping_ratio)
 805        return self._with_eigenvalues(eigenvalues)
 806
 807    def filter_by_index(self, index: int | list[int]) -> Self:
 808        """Keep only the eigenvalue(s) at the given index(es)."""
 809        eigenvalues = self.eigenvalues.filter_by_index(index)
 810        return self._with_eigenvalues(eigenvalues)
 811
 812    def filter_by_state(self, state_names: str | list[str]) -> Self:
 813        """Keep only the given states' participation factors."""
 814        participation_factors = self.participation_factors.filter_by_states(state_names)
 815        return ModalAnalysisResults(
 816            self.sys_matrix,
 817            self.eigenvalues,
 818            participation_factors,
 819            right_eigenvectors=self.right_eigenvectors,
 820            left_eigenvectors=self.left_eigenvectors,
 821        )
 822
 823    def filter_by_min_state_participation(self, min_participation: float) -> Self:
 824        """Keep only states that participate at least `min_participation`
 825        across all eigenvalues currently in this result."""
 826        participation_factors = (
 827            self.participation_factors.filter_by_min_state_participation(
 828                min_participation
 829            )
 830        )
 831        return ModalAnalysisResults(
 832            self.sys_matrix,
 833            self.eigenvalues,
 834            participation_factors,
 835            right_eigenvectors=self.right_eigenvectors,
 836            left_eigenvectors=self.left_eigenvectors,
 837        )
 838
 839    def filter_out_conjugates(self) -> Self:
 840        """Keep only one eigenvalue of each complex-conjugate pair."""
 841        return self._with_eigenvalues(self.eigenvalues.filter_out_conjugates())
 842
 843    def filter_out_real_modes(self) -> Self:
 844        """Keep only the complex (oscillatory) eigenvalues."""
 845        return self._with_eigenvalues(self.eigenvalues.filter_out_real_modes())
 846
 847    def get_system_matrix(self) -> npt.NDArray[np.complex128]:
 848        """The system (state) matrix this result was computed from."""
 849        return self.sys_matrix
 850
 851    def get_states(self) -> npt.NDArray[np.str_]:
 852        """State variable names, as `"<model>\\\\<state variable>"`."""
 853        return self.participation_factors.get_states()
 854
 855    def get_eigenvalues(self) -> EigenvalueSet:
 856        return self.eigenvalues
 857
 858    def get_participation_factors(self) -> ParticipationFactorSet:
 859        return self.participation_factors
 860
 861    def get_right_eigenvectors(self) -> DataFrame | None:
 862        """`(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix of the raw right eigenvectors,
 863        or `None` if this result was built without them."""
 864        return None if self.right_eigenvectors is None else self.right_eigenvectors.copy()
 865
 866    def get_left_eigenvectors(self) -> DataFrame | None:
 867        """`(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix of the raw left eigenvectors,
 868        or `None` if this result was built without them."""
 869        return None if self.left_eigenvectors is None else self.left_eigenvectors.copy()
 870
 871    def eigenvalue_sensitivity(
 872        self, mode_index: int, delta_matrix: npt.NDArray[np.complex128]
 873    ) -> complex:
 874        """Analytical eigenvalue sensitivity `d(lambda)/d(p)` to a
 875        perturbation direction `delta_matrix` (= `dA/dp`) in the state
 876        matrix, via the classical eigenvector-weighted formula
 877
 878            d(lambda_i)/dp = (psi_i^H @ dA/dp @ phi_i) / (psi_i^H @ phi_i)
 879
 880        where `phi_i`/`psi_i` are the right/left eigenvectors of mode
 881        `mode_index` (Perez-Arriaga, Verghese & Schweppe 1982). Unlike
 882        `sensitivity_between` (which finite-differences the *eigenvalues*
 883        between two tracked runs), this is evaluated entirely at this one
 884        operating point - `delta_matrix` is usually itself a finite
 885        difference of the *state matrix* between two runs (see
 886        `system_matrix_sensitivity`), but does not require eigenvalue
 887        tracking, since no eigenvalue comparison across runs is involved.
 888
 889        Args:
 890            mode_index: the eigenvalue (`Index`) to compute the sensitivity for.
 891            delta_matrix: the state-matrix perturbation direction `dA/dp`,
 892                same shape as `get_system_matrix()`.
 893
 894        Returns:
 895            complex: the (generally complex) sensitivity `d(lambda)/dp`. Its
 896            real part is the sensitivity of the eigenvalue's damping; its
 897            imaginary part that of its frequency.
 898        """
 899        if self.right_eigenvectors is None or self.left_eigenvectors is None:
 900            raise PFAttributeNotSetError(
 901                "eigenvectors (this ModalAnalysisResults was built without them - "
 902                "only ModalAnalysis.run()'s results have them)"
 903            )
 904        phi = self.right_eigenvectors[mode_index].to_numpy()
 905        psi = self.left_eigenvectors[mode_index].to_numpy()
 906        numerator = np.vdot(psi, delta_matrix @ phi)
 907        denominator = np.vdot(psi, phi)
 908        return complex(numerator / denominator)
 909
 910    def get_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
 911        """One row per eigenvalue: real/imaginary part, natural/damped
 912        frequency, damping ratio, a `"Mode"` display string and its
 913        `"Dominant states"` (participation >= `DOMINANT_STATES_MIN_PARTICIPATION`)."""
 914        df = self.eigenvalues.get_dataframe().copy()
 915        df[MODE_COL] = df.apply(self._format_mode, axis=1)
 916        df[DOMINANT_STATES_COL] = df.index.map(
 917            lambda idx: ",".join(self._dominant_states(idx))
 918        )
 919        return df
 920
 921    def get_participation_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
 922        """`(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix of participation factors."""
 923        return self.participation_factors.get_dataframe()
 924
 925    def show(self, hide_columns: list[str] | None = None) -> Styler:
 926        """Styled version of `get_dataframe()` - return it as the last
 927        expression of a notebook cell, or pass it to `display()`."""
 928        style = [{"selector": "th", "props": [("vertical-align", "middle")]}]
 929        styled = (
 930            self.get_dataframe()
 931            .style.set_table_styles(style)
 932            .format(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION)
 933            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION)
 934        )
 935        if hide_columns:
 936            styled = styled.hide(hide_columns, axis="columns")
 937        return styled
 938
 939    def show_participation(self) -> Styler:
 940        """Styled version of `get_participation_dataframe()`, with a colour
 941        gradient and the mode string as a second column header level."""
 942        df = self.get_participation_dataframe()
 943        modal_results = self.get_dataframe()
 944        df.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays(
 945            [df.columns, modal_results.loc[df.columns, MODE_COL]],
 946            names=[INDEX_COL, MODE_COL],
 947        )
 948        style = [
 949            {"selector": "th, td", "props": [("text-align", "center")]},
 950        ]
 951        return (
 952            df.style.set_table_styles(style)
 953            .format(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION)
 954            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION)
 955            .background_gradient(axis=None, vmin=0, vmax=1, cmap="YlGnBu")
 956        )
 957
 958    def plot(
 959        self,
 960        ax: plt.Axes | None = None,
 961        *,
 962        xlim: tuple[float, float] | Literal["auto"] | None = "auto",
 963        quantile: float = DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE,
 964    ) -> plt.Axes:
 965        """Scatter the eigenvalues in the complex plane - see
 966        `EigenvalueSet.plot` for `xlim`/`quantile`."""
 967        return self.eigenvalues.plot(ax, xlim=xlim, quantile=quantile)
 968
 969    def plot_participation(self, *, top_n: int | None = 15) -> plt.Figure:
 970        """Bar chart of the participation of every state, one panel per
 971        eigenvalue currently in this result - see
 972        `ParticipationFactorSet.plot` for `top_n`."""
 973        return self.participation_factors.plot(top_n=top_n)
 974
 975    def track_eigenvalues_from(self, other: Self) -> Self:
 976        """Reorder this result's eigenvalues (and participation factors /
 977        eigenvectors) to match the index assigned to the corresponding mode
 978        in `other`."""
 979        index_map = EigenvalueTracker(
 980            other.get_eigenvalues(),
 981            self.get_eigenvalues(),
 982            other.get_participation_factors(),
 983            self.get_participation_factors(),
 984        ).calculate_index_map()
 985        return ModalAnalysisResults(
 986            self.sys_matrix,
 987            self.eigenvalues.map_eigenvalues(index_map),
 988            self.participation_factors.map_eigenvalues(index_map),
 989            right_eigenvectors=self._remap_eigenvectors(self.right_eigenvectors, index_map),
 990            left_eigenvectors=self._remap_eigenvectors(self.left_eigenvectors, index_map),
 991        )
 992
 993    def _with_eigenvalues(self, eigenvalues: EigenvalueSet) -> Self:
 994        """Rebuild with a filtered `EigenvalueSet`, slicing the
 995        participation factors and eigenvectors to match."""
 996        kept = eigenvalues.get_indexes()
 997        return ModalAnalysisResults(
 998            self.sys_matrix,
 999            eigenvalues,
1000            self.participation_factors.filter_by_eigenvalue_index(kept),
1001            right_eigenvectors=self._select_eigenvectors(self.right_eigenvectors, kept),
1002            left_eigenvectors=self._select_eigenvectors(self.left_eigenvectors, kept),
1003        )
1004
1005    @staticmethod
1006    def _select_eigenvectors(df: DataFrame | None, indexes: list[int]) -> DataFrame | None:
1007        return None if df is None else df[indexes]
1008
1009    @staticmethod
1010    def _remap_eigenvectors(
1011        df: DataFrame | None, index_map: dict[int, int]
1012    ) -> DataFrame | None:
1013        return None if df is None else df.rename(columns=index_map)
1014
1015    def _format_mode(self, row: Series) -> str:
1016        if abs(row[IMAG_COL]) < Eigenvalue.EPSILON:
1017            return f"{row[REAL_COL]:.4f}"
1018        return f"{row[REAL_COL]:.4f} ± {abs(row[IMAG_COL]):.4f}j"
1019
1020    def _dominant_states(self, mode_index: int) -> list[str]:
1021        df = self.participation_factors.get_dataframe()
1022        return df.index[
1023            df[mode_index] >= self.DOMINANT_STATES_MIN_PARTICIPATION
1024        ].tolist()
1025
1026    def __len__(self) -> int:
1027        return len(self.eigenvalues)
1028
1029
1030class ModalAnalysis(ApplicationBase):
1031    """Modal (small-signal) analysis of PowerFactory's current state.
1032
1033    Activate the study case / scenario / operating point you want analyzed
1034    yourself first (like `DynamicSimulation` or `StaticCalc` - this class
1035    does not switch study cases for you).
1036    """
1037
1038    #: default `ComMod` parameters: calculate eigenvectors and participation
1039    #: factors and export the system matrix, without dropping any eigenvalue
1040    #: from the results (every 'only record ...' filter switched off).
1041    DEFAULT_COMMOD_PARAMS: dict[str, Any] = {
1042        "iLeft": True,
1043        "iRight": True,
1044        "iPart": True,
1045        "initMode": 0,
1046        "iSysMatsMatl": True,
1047        "isRecOscModesOnly": False,
1048        "isRecUnstabModesOnly": False,
1049        "isRecMinReal": False,
1050        "isRecMaxReal": False,
1051        "isRecMinImag": False,
1052        "isRecMaxImag": False,
1053        "isRecMinMagn": False,
1054        "isRecMaxMagn": False,
1055        "isRecMinDampRat": False,
1056        "isRecMaxDampRat": False,
1057    }
1058
1059    def __init__(self, pf_app: PFApp | None | bool = False, cached: bool = False) -> None:
1060        super().__init__(pf_app, cached)
1061
1062    def run(self, commod_params: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> ModalAnalysisResults:
1063        """Run the modal analysis command (`ComMod`) and return the eigenvalues
1064        and participation factors of the current operating point.
1065
1066        Args:
1067            commod_params: additional/overriding `ComMod` parameters, merged
1068                over `DEFAULT_COMMOD_PARAMS`.
1069
1070        Returns:
1071            ModalAnalysisResults: the eigenvalues, participation factors and
1072            system matrix.
1073        """
1074        export_dir = join(getcwd(), "dynamic_modal_analysis_export")
1075        makedirs(export_dir, exist_ok=True)
1076        try:
1077            self._run_commod(export_dir, commod_params or {})
1078            sys_matrix = self._read_system_matrix(export_dir)
1079            state_names = self._read_state_names(export_dir)
1080        finally:
1081            rmtree(export_dir, ignore_errors=True)
1082
1083        indexes = list(range(1, len(state_names) + 1))
1084        eigenvalue_vec, participation, left_vec, right_vec = self._eigenvalues_and_participation(
1085            sys_matrix
1086        )
1087        eigenvalues = EigenvalueSet(eigenvalue_vec, indexes)
1088        participation_factors = ParticipationFactorSet(participation, state_names, indexes)
1089        right_eigenvectors = pd.DataFrame(right_vec, index=state_names, columns=indexes)
1090        left_eigenvectors = pd.DataFrame(left_vec, index=state_names, columns=indexes)
1091        return ModalAnalysisResults(
1092            sys_matrix,
1093            eigenvalues,
1094            participation_factors,
1095            right_eigenvectors=right_eigenvectors,
1096            left_eigenvectors=left_eigenvectors,
1097        )
1098
1099    def _run_commod(self, export_dir: str, commod_params: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
1100        commod: ComMod = self.act_prj.get_from_study_case("ComMod")
1101        params = {**self.DEFAULT_COMMOD_PARAMS, "dirMatl": export_dir, **commod_params}
1102        self.act_prj.set_attr(commod, params)
1103        commod.Execute()
1104
1105    def _read_system_matrix(self, export_dir: str) -> npt.NDArray[np.complex128]:
1106        """Parse the exported system (A) matrix.
1107
1108        `Amat.mtl` follows the sparse coordinate format MATLAB's `spconvert`
1109        expects: each row is `row column real [imag]`.
1110        """
1111        df = pd.read_csv(
1112            join(export_dir, "Amat.mtl"),
1113            sep=r"\s+",
1114            header=None,
1115            names=["row", "column", "re", "imag"],
1116            dtype={"row": int, "column": int, "re": float, "imag": float},
1117            encoding="ISO-8859-1",
1118            engine="python",
1119        )
1120        size = int(df["row"].max())
1121        sys_matrix = np.zeros((size, size), dtype=np.complex128)
1122        rows = df["row"].to_numpy() - 1
1123        cols = df["column"].to_numpy() - 1
1124        re = df["re"].to_numpy()
1125        imag = df["imag"].to_numpy()
1126        has_imag = ~np.isnan(imag)
1127        sys_matrix[rows[~has_imag], cols[~has_imag]] = re[~has_imag]
1128        sys_matrix[rows[has_imag], cols[has_imag]] = re[has_imag] + 1j * imag[has_imag]
1129        return sys_matrix
1130
1131    def _read_state_names(self, export_dir: str) -> npt.NDArray[np.str_]:
1132        """Parse the exported list of state variable names, as
1133        `"<model name>\\\\<state variable>"`."""
1134        df = pd.read_csv(
1135            join(export_dir, "VariableToIdx_Amat.txt"),
1136            sep=r"\s\s+",
1137            header=0,
1138            names=["Matrix column index", "Model name", "State variable"],
1139            dtype={"Matrix column index": int, "Model name": str, "State variable": str},
1140            encoding="ISO-8859-1",
1141            index_col=0,
1142            engine="python",
1143        )
1144        state_var = df["State variable"].str.replace('"', "", regex=False)
1145        return (df["Model name"] + "\\" + state_var).to_numpy(dtype=str)
1146
1147    def _eigenvalues_and_participation(
1148        self, sys_matrix: npt.NDArray[np.complex128]
1149    ) -> tuple[
1150        npt.NDArray[np.complex128],
1151        npt.NDArray[np.float64],
1152        npt.NDArray[np.complex128],
1153        npt.NDArray[np.complex128],
1154    ]:
1155        """Eigenvalues, the (normalized) participation of every state in
1156        every eigenvalue, and the raw left/right eigenvectors, from one
1157        combined eigendecomposition.
1158
1159        Participation factor `p_ki = |phi_ki| * |psi_ik|` (right eigenvector
1160        element times left eigenvector element), normalized so each
1161        eigenvalue's participation column sums to 1 (Perez-Arriaga et al.) -
1162        the same `phi`/`psi` also used, unnormalized, by
1163        `ModalAnalysisResults.eigenvalue_sensitivity`.
1164        """
1165        eigenvalues, left_vec, right_vec = eig(sys_matrix, left=True, right=True)
1166        participation = np.abs(left_vec) * np.abs(right_vec)
1167        participation = participation / participation.sum(axis=0, keepdims=True)
1168        return eigenvalues, participation, left_vec, right_vec
1169
1170
1171# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
1172# eigenvalue sweeps (built on parstudy.Study)
1173# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
1174
1175
1176class EigenvalueSweepResults:
1177    """How the eigenvalues move as one parameter is swept - the modal-analysis
1178    equivalent of `parstudy.StudyResults`, built from a plain list of
1179    `ModalAnalysisResults` (typically the tracked `raw` results of a
1180    `parstudy.Study` sweep whose `evaluate()` called `ModalAnalysis.run()`;
1181    see `from_study_results` and the tutorial).
1182    """
1183
1184    def __init__(
1185        self, param_values: Sequence[Any], results: Sequence[ModalAnalysisResults]
1186    ) -> None:
1187        if len(param_values) != len(results):
1188            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
1189                f"'param_values' and 'results' must have the same length; got "
1190                f"{len(param_values)} and {len(results)}."
1191            )
1192        self.param_values = list(param_values)
1193        self.results = list(results)
1194
1195    @classmethod
1196    def from_study_results(
1197        cls,
1198        study_results: "StudyResults",
1199        parameter_name: str,
1200        *,
1201        include_baseline: bool = True,
1202    ) -> Self:
1203        """Build from a `parstudy.StudyResults` whose runs' `raw` is a
1204        `ModalAnalysisResults` - i.e. an `evaluate(values)` that returned
1205        `(metrics, modal_analysis.run())`.
1206
1207        Args:
1208            study_results: the `StudyResults` returned by `Study(...).run()`.
1209            parameter_name: name of the swept `parstudy.ModelParameter` whose
1210                value becomes this sweep's parameter axis.
1211            include_baseline: the default `"one_at_a_time"` strategy inserts
1212                one baseline run (every parameter at its default) before the
1213                swept values - set `False` to drop it, e.g. if the swept
1214                range already includes the default value and would otherwise
1215                plot/count it twice.
1216        """
1217        records = study_results.records
1218        if not include_baseline:
1219            records = [r for r in records if r.varied is not None]
1220        param_values = [r.values[parameter_name] for r in records]
1221        results = [study_results.raw(record.index) for record in records]
1222        return cls(param_values, results)
1223
1224    def when(self, param_value: Any) -> ModalAnalysisResults:
1225        """The result run with `parameter == param_value`."""
1226        for value, result in zip(self.param_values, self.results):
1227            if value == param_value:
1228                return result
1229        raise KeyError(f"No result found for parameter value {param_value!r}.")
1230
1231    def when_index(self, run: int) -> ModalAnalysisResults:
1232        """The result at position `run` (0-based, in sweep order)."""
1233        return self.results[run]
1234
1235    def track_eigenvalues(self) -> Self:
1236        """Track eigenvalues across the sweep (each run against the previous)."""
1237        return EigenvalueSweepResults(self.param_values, track_eigenvalues(self.results))
1238
1239    def filter_by_damping_ratio(self, max_damping_ratio: float) -> Self:
1240        results = [r.filter_by_damping_ratio(max_damping_ratio) for r in self.results]
1241        return EigenvalueSweepResults(self.param_values, results)
1242
1243    def filter_by_index(self, index: int | list[int]) -> Self:
1244        results = [r.filter_by_index(index) for r in self.results]
1245        return EigenvalueSweepResults(self.param_values, results)
1246
1247    def filter_out_conjugates(self) -> Self:
1248        results = [r.filter_out_conjugates() for r in self.results]
1249        return EigenvalueSweepResults(self.param_values, results)
1250
1251    def filter_out_real_modes(self) -> Self:
1252        results = [r.filter_out_real_modes() for r in self.results]
1253        return EigenvalueSweepResults(self.param_values, results)
1254
1255    def plot(
1256        self,
1257        *,
1258        colorbar_label: str = "",
1259        ax: plt.Axes | None = None,
1260        xlim: tuple[float, float] | Literal["auto"] | None = "auto",
1261        quantile: float = DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE,
1262    ) -> plt.Axes:
1263        """Scatter every run's eigenvalues in the complex plane, colored by
1264        the parameter value - the classic "root locus" view of a parameter
1265        sweep.
1266
1267        Args:
1268            colorbar_label: label for the parameter-value colorbar.
1269            ax: axes to draw on (a new figure is created if omitted).
1270            xlim: `"auto"` (default) zooms the x-axis to the dominant
1271                eigenvalues (see `EigenvalueSet.plot`), computed across every
1272                run in the sweep; pass an explicit `(lo, hi)` to override, or
1273                `None` for matplotlib's own full-range default.
1274            quantile: only used when `xlim="auto"` - see `EigenvalueSet.plot`.
1275        """
1276        if ax is None:
1277            _, ax = plt.subplots()
1278        max_len = max(len(r) for r in self.results)
1279
1280        real, imag, color = [], [], []
1281        for value, result in zip(self.param_values, self.results):
1282            df = result.get_dataframe()
1283            real.append(self._pad(df[REAL_COL].to_numpy(), max_len))
1284            imag.append(self._pad(df[IMAG_COL].to_numpy(), max_len))
1285            color.append(np.full(max_len, value))
1286
1287        sc = ax.scatter(real, imag, c=color, marker="x", cmap="jet")
1288        if xlim == "auto":
1289            xlim = _auto_real_xlim(np.concatenate(real), quantile=quantile)
1290        if xlim is not None:
1291            ax.set_xlim(xlim)
1292        left, right = ax.get_xlim()
1293        ax.axvspan(0, right, facecolor="red", alpha=0.2)
1294        ax.set_xlim([left, right])
1295        ax.set_xlabel("Real")
1296        ax.set_ylabel("Imaginary")
1297        ax.grid(True)
1298        cbar = ax.figure.colorbar(sc, ax=ax)
1299        cbar.set_label(colorbar_label)
1300        return ax
1301
1302    def plot_eigenvalue_tracking(
1303        self,
1304        ax: plt.Axes | None = None,
1305        *,
1306        xlim: tuple[float, float] | Literal["auto"] | None = "auto",
1307        quantile: float = DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE,
1308        max_legend_entries: int = 20,
1309    ) -> plt.Axes:
1310        """Scatter every run's eigenvalues, colored by eigenvalue *index*
1311        rather than by parameter value - a sanity check that
1312        `track_eigenvalues()` followed each mode correctly (a mode that jumps
1313        discontinuously between runs signals a tracking mistake).
1314
1315        Args:
1316            ax: axes to draw on (a new figure is created if omitted).
1317            xlim: `"auto"` (default) zooms the x-axis to the dominant
1318                eigenvalues (see `EigenvalueSet.plot`); pass an explicit
1319                `(lo, hi)` to override, or `None` for matplotlib's own
1320                full-range default.
1321            quantile: only used when `xlim="auto"` - see `EigenvalueSet.plot`.
1322            max_legend_entries: at most this many eigenvalues - the most
1323                dominant ones, by their largest (least negative) real part
1324                across the sweep - get a legend entry. With every eigenvalue
1325                of a large system otherwise labeled, the legend becomes an
1326                unreadable wall of entries; set to `None` to label all of
1327                them regardless.
1328        """
1329        if ax is None:
1330            _, ax = plt.subplots()
1331        by_index: dict[int, tuple[list[float], list[float]]] = {}
1332        for result in self.results:
1333            for idx, row in result.get_dataframe().iterrows():
1334                real, imag = by_index.setdefault(idx, ([], []))
1335                real.append(row[REAL_COL])
1336                imag.append(row[IMAG_COL])
1337
1338        if xlim == "auto":
1339            all_real = np.concatenate([real for real, _ in by_index.values()])
1340            xlim = _auto_real_xlim(all_real, quantile=quantile)
1341
1342        labeled_indexes: set[int] = set(by_index.keys())
1343        if xlim is not None:
1344            labeled_indexes = {
1345                idx for idx, (real, _) in by_index.items() if max(real) >= xlim[0]
1346            }
1347        if max_legend_entries is not None and len(labeled_indexes) > max_legend_entries:
1348            ranked = sorted(labeled_indexes, key=lambda idx: max(by_index[idx][0]), reverse=True)
1349            labeled_indexes = set(ranked[:max_legend_entries])
1350
1351        for idx, (real, imag) in by_index.items():
1352            ax.scatter(real, imag, marker="x", label=idx if idx in labeled_indexes else None)
1353
1354        if xlim is not None:
1355            ax.set_xlim(xlim)
1356        left, right = ax.get_xlim()
1357        ax.axvspan(0, right, facecolor="red", alpha=0.2)
1358        ax.set_xlim([left, right])
1359        ax.set_xlabel("Real")
1360        ax.set_ylabel("Imaginary")
1361        ax.grid(True)
1362        handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
1363        if handles:
1364            ncol = max(1, math.ceil(len(handles) / 12))
1365            ax.legend(
1366                title=INDEX_COL,
1367                fontsize="small",
1368                ncol=ncol,
1369                loc="upper left",
1370                bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1.0),
1371            )
1372        ax.set_title("Eigenvalue tracking")
1373        return ax
1374
1375    def _pad(self, values: npt.NDArray, size: int) -> npt.NDArray:
1376        if len(values) == size:
1377            return values
1378        return np.pad(values, (0, size - len(values)), constant_values=np.nan)
1379
1380    def __len__(self) -> int:
1381        return len(self.results)
1382
1383
1384# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
1385# modal sensitivity
1386# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
1387
1388
1389class Sensitivity:
1390    """Change in every (tracked) eigenvalue's metrics between two modal
1391    analyses - build with `sensitivity_between`, which tracks the eigenvalues
1392    for you."""
1393
1394    def __init__(
1395        self,
1396        eig_before: EigenvalueSet,
1397        eig_after: EigenvalueSet,
1398        metrics: list[str] | None = None,
1399    ) -> None:
1400        if eig_before.get_indexes() != eig_after.get_indexes():
1401            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
1402                "Eigenvalue indexes must match to compute a sensitivity - "
1403                "track the eigenvalues first (see 'sensitivity_between'). "
1404                f"Got indexes {eig_before.get_indexes()} and {eig_after.get_indexes()}."
1405            )
1406        self.eig_before = eig_before
1407        self.eig_after = eig_after
1408        self.metrics = metrics or []
1409        self.df = eig_after - eig_before
1410        if self.metrics:
1411            self.df = self.df[self.metrics]
1412
1413    def filter_by_metrics(self, metrics: str | list[str]) -> Self:
1414        """Keep only the given eigenvalue metric column(s) (e.g. `"Damping ratio"`)."""
1415        metrics = [metrics] if isinstance(metrics, str) else list(metrics)
1416        return Sensitivity(self.eig_before, self.eig_after, metrics)
1417
1418    def filter_by_index(self, index: int | list[int]) -> Self:
1419        return self._filtered(
1420            self.eig_before.filter_by_index(index), self.eig_after.filter_by_index(index)
1421        )
1422
1423    def filter_by_damping_ratio(self, max_damping_ratio: float) -> Self:
1424        return self._filtered(
1425            self.eig_before.filter_by_damping_ratio(max_damping_ratio),
1426            self.eig_after.filter_by_damping_ratio(max_damping_ratio),
1427        )
1428
1429    def filter_out_conjugates(self) -> Self:
1430        return self._filtered(
1431            self.eig_before.filter_out_conjugates(), self.eig_after.filter_out_conjugates()
1432        )
1433
1434    def filter_out_real_modes(self) -> Self:
1435        return self._filtered(
1436            self.eig_before.filter_out_real_modes(), self.eig_after.filter_out_real_modes()
1437        )
1438
1439    def _filtered(self, eig_before: EigenvalueSet, eig_after: EigenvalueSet) -> Self:
1440        """Restrict both sides to the eigenvalue indexes that independently
1441        passed the filter on *both* sides - a mode can cross from real to
1442        complex (or vice versa) as the swept parameter changes, so filtering
1443        `eig_before` and `eig_after` separately can otherwise leave them with
1444        different indexes."""
1445        common = sorted(set(eig_before.get_indexes()) & set(eig_after.get_indexes()))
1446        return Sensitivity(
1447            eig_before.filter_by_index(common), eig_after.filter_by_index(common), self.metrics
1448        )
1449
1450    def get_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
1451        """`eigenvalue_after - eigenvalue_before` for every metric column,
1452        indexed by (tracked) eigenvalue index."""
1453        return self.df.copy()
1454
1455    def show(self) -> Styler:
1456        """Styled version of `get_dataframe()` - return it as the last
1457        expression of a notebook cell, or pass it to `display()`."""
1458        return (
1459            self.df.style.format(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION)
1460            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION, axis=0)
1461            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION, axis=1)
1462        )
1463
1464
1465def sensitivity_between(
1466    before: ModalAnalysisResults, after: ModalAnalysisResults
1467) -> Sensitivity:
1468    """Sensitivity of every eigenvalue's metrics between two modal analyses.
1469
1470    `after`'s eigenvalues are tracked against `before`'s first, so the
1471    subtraction lines up the same physical mode even if PowerFactory returned
1472    the eigenvalues in a different order.
1473    """
1474    tracked_after = after.track_eigenvalues_from(before)
1475    return Sensitivity(before.get_eigenvalues(), tracked_after.get_eigenvalues())
1476
1477
1478def system_matrix_sensitivity(
1479    before: ModalAnalysisResults, after: ModalAnalysisResults, delta: float
1480) -> npt.NDArray[np.complex128]:
1481    """Finite-difference estimate of `dA/dp`, the state matrix's sensitivity
1482    to a parameter `p`: `(after's state matrix - before's) / delta`, where
1483    `delta` is the change in `p` between the two runs.
1484
1485    Feed the result into `ModalAnalysisResults.eigenvalue_sensitivity` (on
1486    either `before` or `after` - the eigenvectors of both are valid
1487    evaluation points for a small enough `delta`) for the analytical,
1488    eigenvector-weighted eigenvalue sensitivity - see the module docstring
1489    and the *Dynamic Modal Analysis* tutorial for a comparison against
1490    `sensitivity_between`'s finite-difference-on-eigenvalues approach.
1491    """
1492    return (after.get_system_matrix() - before.get_system_matrix()) / delta
1493
1494
1495class ParametricSensitivity:
1496    """Sensitivity across several conditions - e.g. the sensitivity of the
1497    eigenvalues to one parameter, recomputed at several values of a second
1498    ("condition") parameter. Build the list of `Sensitivity` objects yourself
1499    (one `sensitivity_between()` call per condition value - see the tutorial)
1500    and pass them in together with the condition values.
1501    """
1502
1503    def __init__(
1504        self,
1505        condition_values: Sequence[Any],
1506        sensitivities: Sequence[Sensitivity],
1507        normalization: Literal["column", "all"] | None = None,
1508    ) -> None:
1509        if len(condition_values) != len(sensitivities):
1510            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
1511                "'condition_values' and 'sensitivities' must have the same "
1512                f"length; got {len(condition_values)} and {len(sensitivities)}."
1513            )
1514        self.condition_values = list(condition_values)
1515        self.sensitivities = list(sensitivities)
1516        self.normalization = normalization
1517        self.df = self._create_dataframe(
1518            self.condition_values, self.sensitivities
1519        )
1520
1521    def filter_by_metrics(self, metrics: str | list[str]) -> Self:
1522        sensitivities = [s.filter_by_metrics(metrics) for s in self.sensitivities]
1523        return ParametricSensitivity(
1524            self.condition_values, sensitivities, self.normalization
1525        )
1526
1527    def filter_by_index(self, index: int | list[int]) -> Self:
1528        sensitivities = [s.filter_by_index(index) for s in self.sensitivities]
1529        return ParametricSensitivity(
1530            self.condition_values, sensitivities, self.normalization
1531        )
1532
1533    def filter_by_damping_ratio(self, max_damping_ratio: float) -> Self:
1534        sensitivities = [
1535            s.filter_by_damping_ratio(max_damping_ratio) for s in self.sensitivities
1536        ]
1537        return ParametricSensitivity(
1538            self.condition_values, sensitivities, self.normalization
1539        )
1540
1541    def filter_out_conjugates(self) -> Self:
1542        sensitivities = [s.filter_out_conjugates() for s in self.sensitivities]
1543        return ParametricSensitivity(
1544            self.condition_values, sensitivities, self.normalization
1545        )
1546
1547    def filter_out_real_modes(self) -> Self:
1548        sensitivities = [s.filter_out_real_modes() for s in self.sensitivities]
1549        return ParametricSensitivity(
1550            self.condition_values, sensitivities, self.normalization
1551        )
1552
1553    def normalize(self, normalization: Literal["column", "all"]) -> Self:
1554        """Return a copy that `show()`s normalized (0-1) instead of raw values."""
1555        return ParametricSensitivity(
1556            self.condition_values, self.sensitivities, normalization
1557        )
1558
1559    def get_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
1560        return self.df.copy()
1561
1562    def show(self) -> Styler:
1563        """Styled version of `get_dataframe()` (with a colour gradient if
1564        `normalize()` was called) - return it as the last expression of a
1565        notebook cell, or pass it to `display()`."""
1566        df = self.df
1567        match self.normalization:
1568            case "column":
1569                styled = df.div(df.max(axis=1), axis=0).style.background_gradient(
1570                    axis=1, vmin=0, vmax=1, cmap="YlGnBu"
1571                )
1572            case "all":
1573                styled = df.div(df.max(axis=None), axis=0).style.background_gradient(
1574                    axis=None, vmin=0, vmax=1, cmap="YlGnBu"
1575                )
1576            case _:
1577                styled = df.style
1578        return (
1579            styled.format(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION)
1580            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION, axis=0)
1581            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION, axis=1)
1582        )
1583
1584    def _create_dataframe(
1585        self, condition_values: list[Any], sensitivities: list[Sensitivity]
1586    ) -> DataFrame:
1587        df = pd.concat(
1588            [s.get_dataframe() for s in sensitivities], axis=1, keys=condition_values
1589        )
1590        return self._drop_unused_levels(df)
1591
1592    def _drop_unused_levels(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
1593        """Drop MultiIndex levels (rows or columns) that take only one value -
1594        no longer informative once e.g. every sensitivity has the same
1595        eigenvalue indexes."""
1596        result = df.copy()
1597        result.index = self._drop_unused_levels_of(df.index)
1598        result.columns = self._drop_unused_levels_of(df.columns)
1599        return result
1600
1601    def _drop_unused_levels_of(
1602        self, index: pd.MultiIndex | pd.Index
1603    ) -> pd.MultiIndex | pd.Index:
1604        if not isinstance(index, pd.MultiIndex):
1605            return index
1606        result = index
1607        for level in reversed(range(index.nlevels)):
1608            if result.nlevels > 1 and len(index.unique(level=level)) == 1:
1609                result = result.droplevel(level=level)
1610        return result
INDEX_COL = 'Index'
REAL_COL = 'Real (1/s)'
IMAG_COL = 'Imag (rad/s)'
NATURAL_FREQ_COL = 'Undamped natural frequency (Hz)'
DAMPED_FREQ_COL = 'Damped frequency (Hz)'
DAMPING_RATIO_COL = 'Damping ratio'
MODE_COL = 'Mode'
DOMINANT_STATES_COL = 'Dominant states'
DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE = 0.75
class Eigenvalue: 
122class Eigenvalue:
123    """A single eigenvalue of the system state matrix, with the natural
124    frequency, damped frequency and damping ratio derived from it. Immutable.
125    """
126
127    EPSILON = 1e-9
128    "Imaginary part below which an eigenvalue is treated as purely real."
129
130    def __init__(self, value: complex | float, index: int) -> None:
131        """
132        Args:
133            value: the eigenvalue's real and/or imaginary part.
134            index: the eigenvalue's index (1-based, matching PowerFactory's
135                own numbering of the state matrix).
136        """
137        self.index = index
138        self.value = complex(value)
139        self.nat_freq = self._natural_frequency(self.value)
140        self.damp_freq = self._damped_frequency(self.value)
141        self.damp_ratio = self._damping_ratio(self.value)
142
143    def get_index(self) -> int:
144        return self.index
145
146    def get_value(self) -> complex:
147        return self.value
148
149    def get_imag(self) -> float:
150        return self.value.imag
151
152    def get_nat_freq(self) -> float:
153        return self.nat_freq
154
155    def get_damp_ratio(self) -> float:
156        return self.damp_ratio
157
158    def get_series(self) -> Series:
159        """A `Series` with this eigenvalue and the quantities derived from it."""
160        return pd.Series(
161            {
162                INDEX_COL: self.index,
163                REAL_COL: self.value.real,
164                IMAG_COL: self.value.imag,
165                NATURAL_FREQ_COL: self.nat_freq,
166                DAMPED_FREQ_COL: self.damp_freq,
167                DAMPING_RATIO_COL: self.damp_ratio,
168            }
169        )
170
171    def set_index(self, index: int) -> Self:
172        """A copy of this eigenvalue with a different index (does not mutate `self`)."""
173        return Eigenvalue(self.value, index)
174
175    def _damping_ratio(self, eig: complex) -> float:
176        if abs(eig.real) < self.EPSILON and abs(eig.imag) < self.EPSILON:
177            return 1.0
178        return -eig.real / math.sqrt(eig.real**2 + eig.imag**2)
179
180    def _natural_frequency(self, eig: complex) -> float:
181        if abs(eig.imag) < self.EPSILON:
182            return 0.0
183        w_n = math.sqrt(eig.real**2 + eig.imag**2)
184        return w_n / (2 * math.pi)
185
186    def _damped_frequency(self, eig: complex) -> float:
187        w_n = 2 * math.pi * self._natural_frequency(eig)
188        zeta = self._damping_ratio(eig)
189        w_d = w_n * math.sqrt(max(1 - zeta**2, 0.0))
190        return w_d / (2 * math.pi)
191
192    def __lt__(self, other: Self) -> bool:
193        return self.index < other.index
194
195    def __copy__(self) -> Self:
196        return Eigenvalue(self.value, self.index)
197
198    def __repr__(self) -> str:
199        return f"Eigenvalue({self.value.real:.4f}{self.value.imag:+.4f}j, index={self.index})"
