class EigenvalueSet: 
202class EigenvalueSet:
203    """An immutable set of `Eigenvalue`s, e.g. all the eigenvalues of one
204    modal analysis run."""
205
206    def __init__(
207        self,
208        eigenvalues: npt.NDArray | list[Eigenvalue],
209        indexes: int | list[int] | None = None,
210    ) -> None:
211        """
212        Args:
213            eigenvalues: an array of eigenvalues, or a list of `Eigenvalue` objects.
214            indexes: a single index or list of indexes for the eigenvalues.
215                If `eigenvalues` is an array and `indexes` is omitted, they
216                are indexed 1..len(eigenvalues). If a list of `Eigenvalue`
217                objects is passed together with `indexes`, they are reindexed.
218        """
219        indexes = self._handle_indexes(indexes, eigenvalues)
220        if isinstance(eigenvalues, np.ndarray):
221            self.eigenvalues = self._from_array(eigenvalues, indexes)
222        else:
223            self.eigenvalues = self._from_list(eigenvalues, indexes)
224        self.df = self._create_dataframe(self.eigenvalues)
225        self._iter_pos = 0
226
227    def get_indexes(self) -> list[int]:
228        return [e.get_index() for e in self.eigenvalues]
229
230    def get_vector(self) -> npt.NDArray:
231        """The eigenvalues as a complex vector, in index order."""
232        real = self.df[REAL_COL].to_numpy()
233        imag = self.df[IMAG_COL].to_numpy()
234        return real + 1j * imag
235
236    def get_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
237        """One row per eigenvalue: real/imaginary part, natural/damped
238        frequency and damping ratio, indexed by eigenvalue index."""
239        return self.df.copy()
240
241    def filter_by_index(self, indexes: int | list[int]) -> Self:
242        """Keep only the eigenvalues at the given index(es)."""
243        indexes = self._normalize_indexes(indexes)
244        eigenvalues = [e for e in self.eigenvalues if e.get_index() in indexes]
245        return EigenvalueSet(eigenvalues)
246
247    def filter_by_damping_ratio(self, max_damping_ratio: float) -> Self:
248        """Drop eigenvalues whose damping ratio is above `max_damping_ratio`
249        - i.e. keep the poorly-damped/unstable ones."""
250        eigenvalues = [
251            e for e in self.eigenvalues if e.get_damp_ratio() <= max_damping_ratio
252        ]
253        return EigenvalueSet(eigenvalues)
254
255    def filter_out_conjugates(self) -> Self:
256        """Keep only one eigenvalue of each complex-conjugate pair (the one
257        with non-negative imaginary part)."""
258        eigenvalues = [e for e in self.eigenvalues if e.get_imag() >= 0]
259        return EigenvalueSet(eigenvalues)
260
261    def filter_out_real_modes(self) -> Self:
262        """Keep only the complex (oscillatory) eigenvalues."""
263        eigenvalues = [
264            e for e in self.eigenvalues if abs(e.get_imag()) >= Eigenvalue.EPSILON
265        ]
266        return EigenvalueSet(eigenvalues)
267
268    def map_eigenvalues(self, index_map: dict[int, int]) -> Self:
269        """Reindex the eigenvalues according to a map from current to new index."""
270        eigenvalues = [e.set_index(index_map[e.get_index()]) for e in self.eigenvalues]
271        return EigenvalueSet(eigenvalues)
272
273    def plot(
274        self,
275        ax: plt.Axes | None = None,
276        *,
277        xlim: tuple[float, float] | Literal["auto"] | None = "auto",
278        quantile: float = DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE,
279    ) -> plt.Axes:
280        """Scatter the eigenvalues in the complex plane, shading the unstable
281        (right) half-plane.
282
283        Args:
284            ax: axes to draw on (a new figure is created if omitted).
285            xlim: `"auto"` (default) zooms the x-axis to the dominant
286                eigenvalues via `_auto_real_xlim`; pass an explicit `(lo, hi)`
287                to override, or `None` for matplotlib's own full-range default.
288            quantile: only used when `xlim="auto"`. The fraction of
289                eigenvalues (by real part) to zoom *out* past - e.g. the
290                default 0.75 frames roughly the most dominant quarter of
291                eigenvalues; raise it (closer to 1) to zoom in on fewer,
292                more dominant eigenvalues, or lower it to include more of
293                the faster/better-damped ones.
294        """
295        if ax is None:
296            _, ax = plt.subplots()
297        df = self.get_dataframe()
298        ax.scatter(df[REAL_COL], df[IMAG_COL], marker="x")
299        if xlim == "auto":
300            xlim = _auto_real_xlim(df[REAL_COL].to_numpy(), quantile=quantile)
301        if xlim is not None:
302            ax.set_xlim(xlim)
303        left, right = ax.get_xlim()
304        ax.axvspan(0, right, facecolor="red", alpha=0.2)
305        ax.set_xlim([left, right])
306        ax.set_xlabel("Real")
307        ax.set_ylabel("Imaginary")
308        ax.set_title("Eigenvalues")
309        ax.grid(True)
310        return ax
311
312    def _create_dataframe(self, eigenvalues: list[Eigenvalue]) -> DataFrame:
313        return (
314            pd.concat([e.get_series() for e in eigenvalues], axis=1)
315            .T.astype({INDEX_COL: int})
316            .set_index(INDEX_COL)
317        )
318
319    def _handle_indexes(
320        self,
321        indexes: int | list[int] | None,
322        eigenvalues: npt.NDArray | list[Eigenvalue],
323    ) -> list[int] | None:
324        if indexes is None:
325            if isinstance(eigenvalues, np.ndarray):
326                return list(range(1, len(eigenvalues) + 1))
327            return None
328        return self._normalize_indexes(indexes)
329
330    def _normalize_indexes(self, indexes: int | list[int]) -> list[int]:
331        return [indexes] if isinstance(indexes, (int, np.integer)) else list(indexes)
332
333    def _from_array(
334        self, array: npt.NDArray, indexes: list[int]
335    ) -> list[Eigenvalue]:
336        eigenvalues = [Eigenvalue(value, idx) for value, idx in zip(array, indexes)]
337        eigenvalues.sort()
338        return eigenvalues
339
340    def _from_list(
341        self, eigenvalues: list[Eigenvalue], indexes: list[int] | None
342    ) -> list[Eigenvalue]:
343        if indexes:
344            eigenvalues = [e.set_index(idx) for e, idx in zip(eigenvalues, indexes)]
345        eigenvalues = list(eigenvalues)
346        eigenvalues.sort()
347        return eigenvalues
348
349    def __sub__(self, other: Self) -> DataFrame:
350        """Difference of the two sets, column by column (real/imag part,
351        frequencies, damping ratio), row-aligned by eigenvalue index -
352        track_eigenvalues()/track_eigenvalues_from() first if the indexes
353        might not already correspond to the same physical mode."""
354        self_df, other_df = self.get_dataframe(), other.get_dataframe()
355        if len(self_df.index) != len(other_df.index):
356            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
357                "Cannot subtract eigenvalue sets of different length: "
358                f"{len(self_df.index)} vs {len(other_df.index)}."
359            )
360        return self_df - other_df
361
362    def __len__(self) -> int:
363        return len(self.eigenvalues)
364
365    def __iter__(self) -> Self:
366        self._iter_pos = 0
367        return self
368
369    def __next__(self) -> Eigenvalue:
370        if self._iter_pos >= len(self):
371            raise StopIteration
372        e = self.eigenvalues[self._iter_pos]
373        self._iter_pos += 1
374        return e
375
376    def __repr__(self) -> str:
377        return f"EigenvalueSet({np.array2string(self.get_vector(), precision=2, suppress_small=True)})"

class ParticipationFactor: 
380class ParticipationFactor:
381    """The participation of every state in a single eigenvalue."""
382
383    def __init__(
384        self, participation: npt.NDArray, states: npt.NDArray[np.str_], index: int
385    ) -> None:
386        if participation.ndim > 1 or states.ndim > 1:
387            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
388                "'participation' and 'states' must both be one-dimensional; got "
389                f"{participation.ndim} and {states.ndim} dimensions."
390            )
391        self.participation = participation
392        self.states = states
393        self.index = index
394
395    def get_index(self) -> int:
396        return self.index
397
398    def get_array(self) -> npt.NDArray:
399        return self.participation
400
401    def get_series(self) -> Series:
402        # Built from plain lists (not np.insert into self.states) because a
403        # fixed-width numpy string array (e.g. dtype '<U1' for single-char
404        # state names) would silently truncate the "Index" label.
405        index = [INDEX_COL, *self.states.tolist()]
406        values = [self.index, *self.participation.tolist()]
407        return pd.Series(values, index=index)
408
409    def set_index(self, index: int) -> Self:
410        """A copy with a different eigenvalue index (does not mutate `self`)."""
411        return ParticipationFactor(self.participation, self.states, index)
412
413    def filter_by_states(self, states: str | list[str]) -> Self:
414        states_to_keep = {states} if isinstance(states, str) else set(states)
415        mask = np.isin(self.states, list(states_to_keep))
416        return ParticipationFactor(self.participation[mask], self.states[mask], self.index)
417
418    def __lt__(self, other: Self) -> bool:
419        return self.index < other.index

422class ParticipationFactorSet:
423    """Participation factors of every state in every eigenvalue of one modal
424    analysis run - a `(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix."""
425
426    def __init__(
427        self,
428        participations: npt.NDArray | list[ParticipationFactor],
429        states: npt.NDArray[np.str_] | None = None,
430        indexes: int | list[int] | None = None,
431    ) -> None:
432        """
433        Args:
434            participations: a `(state, eigenvalue)` array, or a list of
435                `ParticipationFactor` objects (one per eigenvalue).
436            states: state names - required when `participations` is an array.
437            indexes: eigenvalue indexes (one per column of `participations`).
438                Defaults to 1..n.
439        """
440        indexes = self._handle_indexes(indexes, participations)
441        if isinstance(participations, np.ndarray):
442            if states is None:
443                raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
444                    "'states' must be given when 'participations' is an array."
445                )
446            self.parts = [
447                ParticipationFactor(participations[:, n], states, idx)
448                for n, idx in enumerate(indexes)
449            ]
450            self.parts.sort()
451        else:
452            parts = list(participations)
453            if indexes:
454                parts = [p.set_index(idx) for p, idx in zip(parts, indexes)]
455            parts.sort()
456            self.parts = parts
457        self.df = self._create_dataframe(self.parts)
458        self._iter_pos = 0
459
460    def get_states(self) -> npt.NDArray[np.str_]:
461        return self.df.index.to_numpy()
462
463    def get_array(self) -> npt.NDArray:
464        return self.df.to_numpy()
465
466    def get_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
467        """`(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix of participation factors."""
468        return self.df.copy()
469
470    def filter_by_eigenvalue_index(self, index: int | list[int]) -> Self:
471        indexes = self._normalize_indexes(index)
472        parts = [p for p in self.parts if p.get_index() in indexes]
473        return ParticipationFactorSet(parts)
474
475    def filter_by_states(self, states: str | list[str]) -> Self:
476        parts = [p.filter_by_states(states) for p in self.parts]
477        return ParticipationFactorSet(parts)
478
479    def filter_by_min_state_participation(self, min_participation: float) -> Self:
480        """Keep only states whose participation, summed over every eigenvalue
481        currently in this set, is at least `min_participation`."""
482        totals = self.df.sum(axis=1)
483        states_to_keep = totals.index[totals >= min_participation].tolist()
484        return self.filter_by_states(states_to_keep)
485
486    def map_eigenvalues(self, index_map: dict[int, int]) -> Self:
487        parts = [p.set_index(index_map[p.get_index()]) for p in self.parts]
488        return ParticipationFactorSet(parts)
489
490    def plot(self, *, top_n: int | None = 15) -> plt.Figure:
491        """Horizontal bar chart of the participation of every state - one
492        panel per eigenvalue currently in this set.
493
494        Args:
495            top_n: only the `top_n` states with the highest total
496                participation (summed over every eigenvalue currently in
497                this set) are shown - with many states, showing all of them
498                makes the y-axis labels unreadably crowded. `None` shows
499                every state.
500        """
501        df = self.get_dataframe()
502        if top_n is not None and len(df.index) > top_n:
503            top_states = df.sum(axis=1).sort_values(ascending=False).index[:top_n]
504            df = df.loc[top_states]
505        states = df.index.tolist()
506        y_pos = np.arange(len(states))
507        eigenvalue_indexes = df.columns.tolist()
508        fig, axes = plt.subplots(
509            len(eigenvalue_indexes),
510            1,
511            squeeze=False,
512            figsize=(6, 0.3 * len(states) + 1.2 * len(eigenvalue_indexes)),
513        )
514        for row, idx in enumerate(eigenvalue_indexes):
515            ax = axes[row][0]
516            ax.barh(y_pos, df[idx].to_numpy())
517            ax.set_yticks(y_pos, labels=states, fontsize="small")
518            ax.set_xlabel("Participation")
519            ax.set_title(f"Eigenvalue {idx}")
520        fig.tight_layout()
521        return fig
522
523    def _create_dataframe(self, parts: list[ParticipationFactor]) -> DataFrame:
524        return (
525            pd.concat([p.get_series() for p in parts], axis=1)
526            .T.astype({INDEX_COL: int})
527            .set_index(INDEX_COL)
528            .T
529        )
530
531    def _handle_indexes(
532        self,
533        indexes: int | list[int] | None,
534        participations: npt.NDArray | list[ParticipationFactor],
535    ) -> list[int] | None:
536        if indexes is None:
537            if isinstance(participations, np.ndarray):
538                return list(range(1, participations.shape[1] + 1))
539            return None
540        return self._normalize_indexes(indexes)
541
542    def _normalize_indexes(self, indexes: int | list[int]) -> list[int]:
543        return [indexes] if isinstance(indexes, (int, np.integer)) else list(indexes)
544
545    def __len__(self) -> int:
546        return len(self.parts)
547
548    def __iter__(self) -> Self:
549        self._iter_pos = 0
550        return self
551
552    def __next__(self) -> ParticipationFactor:
553        if self._iter_pos >= len(self):
554            raise StopIteration
555        p = self.parts[self._iter_pos]
556        self._iter_pos += 1
557        return p

class EigenvalueTracker: 
624class EigenvalueTracker:
625    """Reorders a 'scrambled' set of eigenvalues (and matching participation
626    factors) to line up index-for-index with a reference set from another
627    run - PowerFactory does not guarantee eigenvalues come back in the same
628    order between two modal analyses.
629
630    Candidates for "this scrambled eigenvalue is that reference eigenvalue"
631    are scored by three independent distances (nearest eigenvalue in the
632    complex plane, nearest participation-factor vector, nearest natural
633    frequency - the latter weighted up, since it discriminates well between
634    otherwise-similar complex-conjugate-like pairs) and elected by taking the
635    best-scoring pair first, repeatedly, until every position is assigned.
636    """
637
638    #: weight amplifying the natural-frequency distance relative to the
639    #: eigenvalue and participation-factor distances (chosen empirically).
640    NATURAL_FREQUENCY_WEIGHT = 3
641    #: the maximum possible distance between two (normalized) participation vectors.
642    PARTICIPATION_NORMALIZATION = 2
643
644    def __init__(
645        self,
646        eig_ref: EigenvalueSet,
647        eig_scrambled: EigenvalueSet,
648        pf_ref: ParticipationFactorSet,
649        pf_scrambled: ParticipationFactorSet,
650    ) -> None:
651        """
652        Args:
653            eig_ref: eigenvalues of the reference run.
654            eig_scrambled: eigenvalues to reorder to match `eig_ref`.
655            pf_ref: participation factors of the reference run.
656            pf_scrambled: participation factors matching `eig_scrambled`.
657        """
658        if len(eig_ref) != len(eig_scrambled):
659            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
660                f"Length of eigenvalue sets must match to track them: got "
661                f"{len(eig_ref)} and {len(eig_scrambled)}."
662            )
663        self.eig_ref = eig_ref
664        self.eig_scrambled = eig_scrambled
665        self.pf_ref = pf_ref
666        self.pf_scrambled = pf_scrambled
667        self.election = _EigenvaluePositionElection(
668            eig_scrambled.get_indexes(), eig_ref.get_indexes()
669        )
670
671    def calculate_index_map(self) -> dict[int, int]:
672        """Compute the map from `eig_scrambled`'s current indexes to the
673        index of the reference eigenvalue each one is deemed to correspond to."""
674        self._add_eigenvalue_distance_candidates()
675        self._add_participation_distance_candidates()
676        self._add_natural_frequency_distance_candidates()
677        while self.election.elect_best_candidate():
678            pass
679        index_map = self.election.get_winners()
680
681        if len(set(index_map.values())) < len(index_map):
682            raise PFEigenvalueTrackingError(
683                "Eigenvalue tracking is ambiguous: two or more eigenvalues "
684                "would map to the same position.\n"
685                f"Reference eigenvalues: {self.eig_ref!r}\n"
686                f"Scrambled eigenvalues: {self.eig_scrambled!r}\n"
687                f"Index map: {index_map}"
688            )
689        return index_map
690
691    def unscramble(self) -> tuple[EigenvalueSet, ParticipationFactorSet]:
692        """Reorder `eig_scrambled` / `pf_scrambled` to match `eig_ref`'s order."""
693        index_map = self.calculate_index_map()
694        return (
695            self.eig_scrambled.map_eigenvalues(index_map),
696            self.pf_scrambled.map_eigenvalues(index_map),
697        )
698
699    def _add_eigenvalue_distance_candidates(self) -> None:
700        for eig in self.eig_scrambled:
701            candidates = [
702                _IndexCandidate(
703                    eig.get_index(),
704                    ref.get_index(),
705                    -abs(ref.get_value() - eig.get_value()),
706                )
707                for ref in self.eig_ref
708            ]
709            self.election.add_candidates(candidates)
710
711    def _add_participation_distance_candidates(self) -> None:
712        for pf in self.pf_scrambled:
713            candidates = [
714                _IndexCandidate(
715                    pf.get_index(),
716                    ref.get_index(),
717                    -np.linalg.norm(ref.get_array() - pf.get_array())
718                    / self.PARTICIPATION_NORMALIZATION,
719                )
720                for ref in self.pf_ref
721            ]
722            self.election.add_candidates(candidates)
723
724    def _add_natural_frequency_distance_candidates(self) -> None:
725        for eig in self.eig_scrambled:
726            candidates = [
727                _IndexCandidate(
728                    eig.get_index(),
729                    ref.get_index(),
730                    -abs(ref.get_nat_freq() - eig.get_nat_freq())
731                    * self.NATURAL_FREQUENCY_WEIGHT,
732                )
733                for ref in self.eig_ref
734            ]
735            self.election.add_candidates(candidates)

def track_eigenvalues( results: Sequence[ModalAnalysisResults]) -> list[ModalAnalysisResults]: 
738def track_eigenvalues(results: Sequence["ModalAnalysisResults"]) -> list["ModalAnalysisResults"]:
739    """Track eigenvalues across a sequence of modal analysis runs (e.g. the
740    `raw` results of a `parstudy.Study` sweep), so every result's eigenvalue
741    index consistently refers to the same physical mode.
742
743    Each result is tracked against the *previous* (already-tracked) one, not
744    against the first, so a mode can drift gradually across many runs without
745    ever being compared to a very different reference.
746
747    Args:
748        results: the modal analysis results in run order. The first is kept
749            as-is and used as the initial reference.
750
751    Returns:
752        A new list of `ModalAnalysisResults`, reindexed to be consistent
753        with one another.
754    """
755    tracked: list[ModalAnalysisResults] = []
756    for i, result in enumerate(results):
757        if i == 0:
758            tracked.append(result)
759        else:
760            tracked.append(result.track_eigenvalues_from(tracked[-1]))
761    return tracked

Track eigenvalues across a sequence of modal analysis runs (e.g. the raw results of a parstudy.Study sweep), so every result's eigenvalue index consistently refers to the same physical mode.

Each result is tracked against the previous (already-tracked) one, not against the first, so a mode can drift gradually across many runs without ever being compared to a very different reference.

Args: results: the modal analysis results in run order. The first is kept as-is and used as the initial reference.

Returns: A new list of ModalAnalysisResults, reindexed to be consistent with one another.

class ModalAnalysisResults: 
 769class ModalAnalysisResults:
 770    """Result of one modal analysis run: eigenvalues, participation factors
 771    and the system (state) matrix they were computed from."""
 772
 773    #: minimum participation for a state to be listed as "dominant" for a mode.
 774    DOMINANT_STATES_MIN_PARTICIPATION = 0.05
 775
 776    def __init__(
 777        self,
 778        sys_matrix: npt.NDArray[np.complex128],
 779        eigenvalues: EigenvalueSet,
 780        participation_factors: ParticipationFactorSet,
 781        *,
 782        right_eigenvectors: DataFrame | None = None,
 783        left_eigenvectors: DataFrame | None = None,
 784    ) -> None:
 785        """
 786        Args:
 787            sys_matrix: the system (state) matrix.
 788            eigenvalues: the eigenvalues.
 789            participation_factors: participation of every state in every eigenvalue.
 790            right_eigenvectors: `(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix of the raw
 791                (complex, unnormalized) right eigenvectors - needed for
 792                `eigenvalue_sensitivity`. `None` if not computed (e.g. a
 793                `ModalAnalysisResults` built by hand without them).
 794            left_eigenvectors: the matching left eigenvectors.
 795        """
 796        self.sys_matrix = sys_matrix
 797        self.eigenvalues = eigenvalues
 798        self.participation_factors = participation_factors
 799        self.right_eigenvectors = right_eigenvectors
 800        self.left_eigenvectors = left_eigenvectors
 801
 802    def filter_by_damping_ratio(self, max_damping_ratio: float) -> Self:
 803        """Keep only the eigenvalues with a damping ratio at or below
 804        `max_damping_ratio` - i.e. the poorly-damped/unstable ones."""
 805        eigenvalues = self.eigenvalues.filter_by_damping_ratio(max_damping_ratio)
 806        return self._with_eigenvalues(eigenvalues)
 807
 808    def filter_by_index(self, index: int | list[int]) -> Self:
 809        """Keep only the eigenvalue(s) at the given index(es)."""
 810        eigenvalues = self.eigenvalues.filter_by_index(index)
 811        return self._with_eigenvalues(eigenvalues)
 812
 813    def filter_by_state(self, state_names: str | list[str]) -> Self:
 814        """Keep only the given states' participation factors."""
 815        participation_factors = self.participation_factors.filter_by_states(state_names)
 816        return ModalAnalysisResults(
 817            self.sys_matrix,
 818            self.eigenvalues,
 819            participation_factors,
 820            right_eigenvectors=self.right_eigenvectors,
 821            left_eigenvectors=self.left_eigenvectors,
 822        )
 823
 824    def filter_by_min_state_participation(self, min_participation: float) -> Self:
 825        """Keep only states that participate at least `min_participation`
 826        across all eigenvalues currently in this result."""
 827        participation_factors = (
 828            self.participation_factors.filter_by_min_state_participation(
 829                min_participation
 830            )
 831        )
 832        return ModalAnalysisResults(
 833            self.sys_matrix,
 834            self.eigenvalues,
 835            participation_factors,
 836            right_eigenvectors=self.right_eigenvectors,
 837            left_eigenvectors=self.left_eigenvectors,
 838        )

 858
 859    def get_participation_factors(self) -> ParticipationFactorSet:

 862    def get_right_eigenvectors(self) -> DataFrame | None:
 863        """`(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix of the raw right eigenvectors,
 864        or `None` if this result was built without them."""
 865        return None if self.right_eigenvectors is None else self.right_eigenvectors.copy()
 866
 867    def get_left_eigenvectors(self) -> DataFrame | None:
 868        """`(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix of the raw left eigenvectors,
 869        or `None` if this result was built without them."""
 870        return None if self.left_eigenvectors is None else self.left_eigenvectors.copy()
 871
 872    def eigenvalue_sensitivity(
 873        self, mode_index: int, delta_matrix: npt.NDArray[np.complex128]
 874    ) -> complex:
 875        """Analytical eigenvalue sensitivity `d(lambda)/d(p)` to a
 876        perturbation direction `delta_matrix` (= `dA/dp`) in the state
 877        matrix, via the classical eigenvector-weighted formula
 878
 879            d(lambda_i)/dp = (psi_i^H @ dA/dp @ phi_i) / (psi_i^H @ phi_i)
 880
 881        where `phi_i`/`psi_i` are the right/left eigenvectors of mode
 882        `mode_index` (Perez-Arriaga, Verghese & Schweppe 1982). Unlike
 883        `sensitivity_between` (which finite-differences the *eigenvalues*
 884        between two tracked runs), this is evaluated entirely at this one
 885        operating point - `delta_matrix` is usually itself a finite
 886        difference of the *state matrix* between two runs (see
 887        `system_matrix_sensitivity`), but does not require eigenvalue
 888        tracking, since no eigenvalue comparison across runs is involved.
 889
 890        Args:
 891            mode_index: the eigenvalue (`Index`) to compute the sensitivity for.
 892            delta_matrix: the state-matrix perturbation direction `dA/dp`,
 893                same shape as `get_system_matrix()`.
 894
 895        Returns:
 896            complex: the (generally complex) sensitivity `d(lambda)/dp`. Its
 897            real part is the sensitivity of the eigenvalue's damping; its
 898            imaginary part that of its frequency.
 899        """
 900        if self.right_eigenvectors is None or self.left_eigenvectors is None:
 901            raise PFAttributeNotSetError(
 902                "eigenvectors (this ModalAnalysisResults was built without them - "
 903                "only ModalAnalysis.run()'s results have them)"
 904            )
 905        phi = self.right_eigenvectors[mode_index].to_numpy()
 906        psi = self.left_eigenvectors[mode_index].to_numpy()
 907        numerator = np.vdot(psi, delta_matrix @ phi)
 908        denominator = np.vdot(psi, phi)
 909        return complex(numerator / denominator)
 910
 911    def get_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
 912        """One row per eigenvalue: real/imaginary part, natural/damped
 913        frequency, damping ratio, a `"Mode"` display string and its
 914        `"Dominant states"` (participation >= `DOMINANT_STATES_MIN_PARTICIPATION`)."""
 915        df = self.eigenvalues.get_dataframe().copy()
 916        df[MODE_COL] = df.apply(self._format_mode, axis=1)
 917        df[DOMINANT_STATES_COL] = df.index.map(
 918            lambda idx: ",".join(self._dominant_states(idx))
 919        )
 920        return df
 921
 922    def get_participation_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
 923        """`(state, eigenvalue index)` matrix of participation factors."""
 924        return self.participation_factors.get_dataframe()

 926    def show(self, hide_columns: list[str] | None = None) -> Styler:
 927        """Styled version of `get_dataframe()` - return it as the last

 929        style = [{"selector": "th", "props": [("vertical-align", "middle")]}]
 930        styled = (
 931            self.get_dataframe()
 932            .style.set_table_styles(style)
 933            .format(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION)
 934            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION)
 935        )
 936        if hide_columns:
 937            styled = styled.hide(hide_columns, axis="columns")
 938        return styled

 941        """Styled version of `get_participation_dataframe()`, with a colour
 942        gradient and the mode string as a second column header level."""
 943        df = self.get_participation_dataframe()
 944        modal_results = self.get_dataframe()
 945        df.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_arrays(
 946            [df.columns, modal_results.loc[df.columns, MODE_COL]],
 947            names=[INDEX_COL, MODE_COL],
 948        )
 949        style = [
 950            {"selector": "th, td", "props": [("text-align", "center")]},
 951        ]
 952        return (

 957        )

 960        self,

 964        quantile: float = DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE,
 965    ) -> plt.Axes:
 966        """Scatter the eigenvalues in the complex plane - see

 970    def plot_participation(self, *, top_n: int | None = 15) -> plt.Figure:
 971        """Bar chart of the participation of every state, one panel per
 972        eigenvalue currently in this result - see

 976    def track_eigenvalues_from(self, other: Self) -> Self:
 977        """Reorder this result's eigenvalues (and participation factors /
 978        eigenvectors) to match the index assigned to the corresponding mode
 979        in `other`."""
 980        index_map = EigenvalueTracker(
 981            other.get_eigenvalues(),
 982            self.get_eigenvalues(),
 983            other.get_participation_factors(),
 984            self.get_participation_factors(),
 985        ).calculate_index_map()
 986        return ModalAnalysisResults(
 987            self.sys_matrix,
 988            self.eigenvalues.map_eigenvalues(index_map),
 989            self.participation_factors.map_eigenvalues(index_map),
 990            right_eigenvectors=self._remap_eigenvectors(self.right_eigenvectors, index_map),
 991            left_eigenvectors=self._remap_eigenvectors(self.left_eigenvectors, index_map),
 992        )
 993
 994    def _with_eigenvalues(self, eigenvalues: EigenvalueSet) -> Self:
 995        """Rebuild with a filtered `EigenvalueSet`, slicing the
 996        participation factors and eigenvectors to match."""
 997        kept = eigenvalues.get_indexes()
 998        return ModalAnalysisResults(
 999            self.sys_matrix,
1000            eigenvalues,
1001            self.participation_factors.filter_by_eigenvalue_index(kept),
1002            right_eigenvectors=self._select_eigenvectors(self.right_eigenvectors, kept),
1003            left_eigenvectors=self._select_eigenvectors(self.left_eigenvectors, kept),
1004        )
1005
1006    @staticmethod
1007    def _select_eigenvectors(df: DataFrame | None, indexes: list[int]) -> DataFrame | None:
1008        return None if df is None else df[indexes]
1009
1010    @staticmethod
1011    def _remap_eigenvectors(
1012        df: DataFrame | None, index_map: dict[int, int]
1013    ) -> DataFrame | None:
1014        return None if df is None else df.rename(columns=index_map)
1015
1016    def _format_mode(self, row: Series) -> str:
1017        if abs(row[IMAG_COL]) < Eigenvalue.EPSILON:
1018            return f"{row[REAL_COL]:.4f}"
1019        return f"{row[REAL_COL]:.4f} ± {abs(row[IMAG_COL]):.4f}j"
1020
1021    def _dominant_states(self, mode_index: int) -> list[str]:
1022        df = self.participation_factors.get_dataframe()
1023        return df.index[
1024            df[mode_index] >= self.DOMINANT_STATES_MIN_PARTICIPATION
1025        ].tolist()
1026
1027    def __len__(self) -> int:
1028        return len(self.eigenvalues)

class ModalAnalysis(powfacpy.applications.application_base.ApplicationBase): 
1031class ModalAnalysis(ApplicationBase):
1032    """Modal (small-signal) analysis of PowerFactory's current state.
1033
1034    Activate the study case / scenario / operating point you want analyzed
1035    yourself first (like `DynamicSimulation` or `StaticCalc` - this class
1036    does not switch study cases for you).
1037    """
1038
1039    #: default `ComMod` parameters: calculate eigenvectors and participation
1040    #: factors and export the system matrix, without dropping any eigenvalue
1041    #: from the results (every 'only record ...' filter switched off).
1042    DEFAULT_COMMOD_PARAMS: dict[str, Any] = {
1043        "iLeft": True,
1044        "iRight": True,
1045        "iPart": True,
1046        "initMode": 0,
1047        "iSysMatsMatl": True,
1048        "isRecOscModesOnly": False,
1049        "isRecUnstabModesOnly": False,
1050        "isRecMinReal": False,
1051        "isRecMaxReal": False,
1052        "isRecMinImag": False,
1053        "isRecMaxImag": False,
1054        "isRecMinMagn": False,
1055        "isRecMaxMagn": False,
1056        "isRecMinDampRat": False,
1057        "isRecMaxDampRat": False,
1058    }

1060    def __init__(self, pf_app: PFApp | None | bool = False, cached: bool = False) -> None:
1061        super().__init__(pf_app, cached)

1063    def run(self, commod_params: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> ModalAnalysisResults:
1064        """Run the modal analysis command (`ComMod`) and return the eigenvalues
1065        and participation factors of the current operating point.
1066
1067        Args:
1068            commod_params: additional/overriding `ComMod` parameters, merged
1069                over `DEFAULT_COMMOD_PARAMS`.
1070
1071        Returns:
1072            ModalAnalysisResults: the eigenvalues, participation factors and
1073            system matrix.
1074        """
1075        export_dir = join(getcwd(), "dynamic_modal_analysis_export")
1076        makedirs(export_dir, exist_ok=True)
1077        try:
1078            self._run_commod(export_dir, commod_params or {})
1079            sys_matrix = self._read_system_matrix(export_dir)
1080            state_names = self._read_state_names(export_dir)
1081        finally:
1082            rmtree(export_dir, ignore_errors=True)
1083
1084        indexes = list(range(1, len(state_names) + 1))
1085        eigenvalue_vec, participation, left_vec, right_vec = self._eigenvalues_and_participation(
1086            sys_matrix
1087        )
1088        eigenvalues = EigenvalueSet(eigenvalue_vec, indexes)
1089        participation_factors = ParticipationFactorSet(participation, state_names, indexes)
1090        right_eigenvectors = pd.DataFrame(right_vec, index=state_names, columns=indexes)
1091        left_eigenvectors = pd.DataFrame(left_vec, index=state_names, columns=indexes)
1092        return ModalAnalysisResults(
1093            sys_matrix,
1094            eigenvalues,
1095            participation_factors,
1096            right_eigenvectors=right_eigenvectors,
1097            left_eigenvectors=left_eigenvectors,
1098        )
1099
1100    def _run_commod(self, export_dir: str, commod_params: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
1101        commod: ComMod = self.act_prj.get_from_study_case("ComMod")
1102        params = {**self.DEFAULT_COMMOD_PARAMS, "dirMatl": export_dir, **commod_params}
1103        self.act_prj.set_attr(commod, params)
1104        commod.Execute()
1105
1106    def _read_system_matrix(self, export_dir: str) -> npt.NDArray[np.complex128]:
1107        """Parse the exported system (A) matrix.
1108
1109        `Amat.mtl` follows the sparse coordinate format MATLAB's `spconvert`
1110        expects: each row is `row column real [imag]`.
1111        """
1112        df = pd.read_csv(
1113            join(export_dir, "Amat.mtl"),
1114            sep=r"\s+",
1115            header=None,
1116            names=["row", "column", "re", "imag"],
1117            dtype={"row": int, "column": int, "re": float, "imag": float},
1118            encoding="ISO-8859-1",
1119            engine="python",
1120        )
1121        size = int(df["row"].max())
1122        sys_matrix = np.zeros((size, size), dtype=np.complex128)
1123        rows = df["row"].to_numpy() - 1
1124        cols = df["column"].to_numpy() - 1
1125        re = df["re"].to_numpy()
1126        imag = df["imag"].to_numpy()
1127        has_imag = ~np.isnan(imag)
1128        sys_matrix[rows[~has_imag], cols[~has_imag]] = re[~has_imag]
1129        sys_matrix[rows[has_imag], cols[has_imag]] = re[has_imag] + 1j * imag[has_imag]
1130        return sys_matrix
1131
1132    def _read_state_names(self, export_dir: str) -> npt.NDArray[np.str_]:
1133        """Parse the exported list of state variable names, as
1134        `"<model name>\\\\<state variable>"`."""
1135        df = pd.read_csv(
1136            join(export_dir, "VariableToIdx_Amat.txt"),
1137            sep=r"\s\s+",
1138            header=0,
1139            names=["Matrix column index", "Model name", "State variable"],
1140            dtype={"Matrix column index": int, "Model name": str, "State variable": str},
1141            encoding="ISO-8859-1",
1142            index_col=0,
1143            engine="python",
1144        )
1145        state_var = df["State variable"].str.replace('"', "", regex=False)
1146        return (df["Model name"] + "\\" + state_var).to_numpy(dtype=str)
1147
1148    def _eigenvalues_and_participation(
1149        self, sys_matrix: npt.NDArray[np.complex128]
1150    ) -> tuple[
1151        npt.NDArray[np.complex128],
1152        npt.NDArray[np.float64],
1153        npt.NDArray[np.complex128],
1154        npt.NDArray[np.complex128],
1155    ]:
1156        """Eigenvalues, the (normalized) participation of every state in
1157        every eigenvalue, and the raw left/right eigenvectors, from one
1158        combined eigendecomposition.
1159
1160        Participation factor `p_ki = |phi_ki| * |psi_ik|` (right eigenvector
1161        element times left eigenvector element), normalized so each
1162        eigenvalue's participation column sums to 1 (Perez-Arriaga et al.) -
1163        the same `phi`/`psi` also used, unnormalized, by
1164        `ModalAnalysisResults.eigenvalue_sensitivity`.
1165        """
1166        eigenvalues, left_vec, right_vec = eig(sys_matrix, left=True, right=True)
1167        participation = np.abs(left_vec) * np.abs(right_vec)
1168        participation = participation / participation.sum(axis=0, keepdims=True)
1169        return eigenvalues, participation, left_vec, right_vec

1177class EigenvalueSweepResults:
1178    """How the eigenvalues move as one parameter is swept - the modal-analysis
1179    equivalent of `parstudy.StudyResults`, built from a plain list of
1180    `ModalAnalysisResults` (typically the tracked `raw` results of a
1181    `parstudy.Study` sweep whose `evaluate()` called `ModalAnalysis.run()`;
1182    see `from_study_results` and the tutorial).
1183    """
1184
1185    def __init__(
1186        self, param_values: Sequence[Any], results: Sequence[ModalAnalysisResults]
1187    ) -> None:
1188        if len(param_values) != len(results):
1189            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
1190                f"'param_values' and 'results' must have the same length; got "
1191                f"{len(param_values)} and {len(results)}."
1192            )
1193        self.param_values = list(param_values)
1194        self.results = list(results)
1195
1196    @classmethod
1197    def from_study_results(
1198        cls,
1199        study_results: "StudyResults",
1200        parameter_name: str,
1201        *,
1202        include_baseline: bool = True,
1203    ) -> Self:
1204        """Build from a `parstudy.StudyResults` whose runs' `raw` is a
1205        `ModalAnalysisResults` - i.e. an `evaluate(values)` that returned
1206        `(metrics, modal_analysis.run())`.
1207
1208        Args:
1209            study_results: the `StudyResults` returned by `Study(...).run()`.
1210            parameter_name: name of the swept `parstudy.ModelParameter` whose
1211                value becomes this sweep's parameter axis.
1212            include_baseline: the default `"one_at_a_time"` strategy inserts
1213                one baseline run (every parameter at its default) before the
1214                swept values - set `False` to drop it, e.g. if the swept
1215                range already includes the default value and would otherwise
1216                plot/count it twice.
1217        """
1218        records = study_results.records
1219        if not include_baseline:
1220            records = [r for r in records if r.varied is not None]
1221        param_values = [r.values[parameter_name] for r in records]
1222        results = [study_results.raw(record.index) for record in records]
1223        return cls(param_values, results)

1229                return result
1230        raise KeyError(f"No result found for parameter value {param_value!r}.")

1233        """The result at position `run` (0-based, in sweep order)."""
1234        return self.results[run]

1256    def plot(
1257        self,
1258        *,
1259        colorbar_label: str = "",
1260        ax: plt.Axes | None = None,

1264        """Scatter every run's eigenvalues in the complex plane, colored by

1285            imag.append(self._pad(df[IMAG_COL].to_numpy(), max_len))
1286            color.append(np.full(max_len, value))
1287
1288        sc = ax.scatter(real, imag, c=color, marker="x", cmap="jet")
1289        if xlim == "auto":
1290            xlim = _auto_real_xlim(np.concatenate(real), quantile=quantile)
1291        if xlim is not None:
1292            ax.set_xlim(xlim)
1293        left, right = ax.get_xlim()
1294        ax.axvspan(0, right, facecolor="red", alpha=0.2)
1295        ax.set_xlim([left, right])
1296        ax.set_xlabel("Real")
1297        ax.set_ylabel("Imaginary")
1298        ax.grid(True)
1299        cbar = ax.figure.colorbar(sc, ax=ax)
1300        cbar.set_label(colorbar_label)
1301        return ax
1302
1303    def plot_eigenvalue_tracking(
1304        self,
1305        ax: plt.Axes | None = None,
1306        *,
1307        xlim: tuple[float, float] | Literal["auto"] | None = "auto",
1308        quantile: float = DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE,
1309        max_legend_entries: int = 20,
1310    ) -> plt.Axes:
1311        """Scatter every run's eigenvalues, colored by eigenvalue *index*
1312        rather than by parameter value - a sanity check that
1313        `track_eigenvalues()` followed each mode correctly (a mode that jumps
1314        discontinuously between runs signals a tracking mistake).
1315
1316        Args:
1317            ax: axes to draw on (a new figure is created if omitted).
1318            xlim: `"auto"` (default) zooms the x-axis to the dominant
1319                eigenvalues (see `EigenvalueSet.plot`); pass an explicit
1320                `(lo, hi)` to override, or `None` for matplotlib's own
1321                full-range default.
1322            quantile: only used when `xlim="auto"` - see `EigenvalueSet.plot`.
1323            max_legend_entries: at most this many eigenvalues - the most
1324                dominant ones, by their largest (least negative) real part
1325                across the sweep - get a legend entry. With every eigenvalue
1326                of a large system otherwise labeled, the legend becomes an
1327                unreadable wall of entries; set to `None` to label all of
1328                them regardless.
1329        """
1330        if ax is None:
1331            _, ax = plt.subplots()
1332        by_index: dict[int, tuple[list[float], list[float]]] = {}
1333        for result in self.results:
1334            for idx, row in result.get_dataframe().iterrows():
1335                real, imag = by_index.setdefault(idx, ([], []))
1336                real.append(row[REAL_COL])
1337                imag.append(row[IMAG_COL])
1338
1339        if xlim == "auto":
1340            all_real = np.concatenate([real for real, _ in by_index.values()])
1341            xlim = _auto_real_xlim(all_real, quantile=quantile)
1342
1343        labeled_indexes: set[int] = set(by_index.keys())
1344        if xlim is not None:
1345            labeled_indexes = {
1346                idx for idx, (real, _) in by_index.items() if max(real) >= xlim[0]
1347            }
1348        if max_legend_entries is not None and len(labeled_indexes) > max_legend_entries:
1349            ranked = sorted(labeled_indexes, key=lambda idx: max(by_index[idx][0]), reverse=True)
1350            labeled_indexes = set(ranked[:max_legend_entries])
1351
1352        for idx, (real, imag) in by_index.items():
1353            ax.scatter(real, imag, marker="x", label=idx if idx in labeled_indexes else None)
1354
1355        if xlim is not None:
1356            ax.set_xlim(xlim)
1357        left, right = ax.get_xlim()
1358        ax.axvspan(0, right, facecolor="red", alpha=0.2)
1359        ax.set_xlim([left, right])
1360        ax.set_xlabel("Real")
1361        ax.set_ylabel("Imaginary")
1362        ax.grid(True)
1363        handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
1364        if handles:
1365            ncol = max(1, math.ceil(len(handles) / 12))
1366            ax.legend(
1367                title=INDEX_COL,
1368                fontsize="small",
1369                ncol=ncol,
1370                loc="upper left",
1371                bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1.0),
1372            )
1373        ax.set_title("Eigenvalue tracking")
1374        return ax
1375
1376    def _pad(self, values: npt.NDArray, size: int) -> npt.NDArray:
1377        if len(values) == size:
1378            return values
1379        return np.pad(values, (0, size - len(values)), constant_values=np.nan)
1380
1381    def __len__(self) -> int:
1382        return len(self.results)

1286            color.append(np.full(max_len, value))
1287
1288        sc = ax.scatter(real, imag, c=color, marker="x", cmap="jet")
1289        if xlim == "auto":
1290            xlim = _auto_real_xlim(np.concatenate(real), quantile=quantile)
1291        if xlim is not None:
1292            ax.set_xlim(xlim)
1293        left, right = ax.get_xlim()
1294        ax.axvspan(0, right, facecolor="red", alpha=0.2)
1295        ax.set_xlim([left, right])
1296        ax.set_xlabel("Real")
1297        ax.set_ylabel("Imaginary")
1298        ax.grid(True)
1299        cbar = ax.figure.colorbar(sc, ax=ax)
1300        cbar.set_label(colorbar_label)
1301        return ax

Scatter every run's eigenvalues in the complex plane, colored by the parameter value - the classic "root locus" view of a parameter sweep.

Args: colorbar_label: label for the parameter-value colorbar. ax: axes to draw on (a new figure is created if omitted). xlim: "auto" (default) zooms the x-axis to the dominant eigenvalues (see EigenvalueSet.plot), computed across every run in the sweep; pass an explicit (lo, hi) to override, or None for matplotlib's own full-range default. quantile: only used when xlim="auto" - see EigenvalueSet.plot.

def plot_eigenvalue_tracking( self, ax: matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes | None = None, *, xlim: Union[tuple[float, float], Literal['auto'], NoneType] = 'auto', quantile: float = 0.75, max_legend_entries: int = 20) -> matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes: 
1303    def plot_eigenvalue_tracking(
1304        self,
1305        ax: plt.Axes | None = None,
1306        *,
1307        xlim: tuple[float, float] | Literal["auto"] | None = "auto",
1308        quantile: float = DEFAULT_DOMINANT_QUANTILE,
1309        max_legend_entries: int = 20,
1310    ) -> plt.Axes:
1311        """Scatter every run's eigenvalues, colored by eigenvalue *index*
1312        rather than by parameter value - a sanity check that
1313        `track_eigenvalues()` followed each mode correctly (a mode that jumps
1314        discontinuously between runs signals a tracking mistake).
1315
1316        Args:
1317            ax: axes to draw on (a new figure is created if omitted).
1318            xlim: `"auto"` (default) zooms the x-axis to the dominant
1319                eigenvalues (see `EigenvalueSet.plot`); pass an explicit
1320                `(lo, hi)` to override, or `None` for matplotlib's own
1321                full-range default.
1322            quantile: only used when `xlim="auto"` - see `EigenvalueSet.plot`.
1323            max_legend_entries: at most this many eigenvalues - the most
1324                dominant ones, by their largest (least negative) real part
1325                across the sweep - get a legend entry. With every eigenvalue
1326                of a large system otherwise labeled, the legend becomes an
1327                unreadable wall of entries; set to `None` to label all of
1328                them regardless.
1329        """
1330        if ax is None:
1331            _, ax = plt.subplots()
1332        by_index: dict[int, tuple[list[float], list[float]]] = {}
1333        for result in self.results:
1334            for idx, row in result.get_dataframe().iterrows():
1335                real, imag = by_index.setdefault(idx, ([], []))
1336                real.append(row[REAL_COL])
1337                imag.append(row[IMAG_COL])
1338
1339        if xlim == "auto":
1340            all_real = np.concatenate([real for real, _ in by_index.values()])
1341            xlim = _auto_real_xlim(all_real, quantile=quantile)
1342
1343        labeled_indexes: set[int] = set(by_index.keys())
1344        if xlim is not None:
1345            labeled_indexes = {
1346                idx for idx, (real, _) in by_index.items() if max(real) >= xlim[0]
1347            }
1348        if max_legend_entries is not None and len(labeled_indexes) > max_legend_entries:
1349            ranked = sorted(labeled_indexes, key=lambda idx: max(by_index[idx][0]), reverse=True)
1350            labeled_indexes = set(ranked[:max_legend_entries])
1351
1352        for idx, (real, imag) in by_index.items():
1353            ax.scatter(real, imag, marker="x", label=idx if idx in labeled_indexes else None)
1354
1355        if xlim is not None:
1356            ax.set_xlim(xlim)
1357        left, right = ax.get_xlim()
1358        ax.axvspan(0, right, facecolor="red", alpha=0.2)
1359        ax.set_xlim([left, right])
1360        ax.set_xlabel("Real")
1361        ax.set_ylabel("Imaginary")
1362        ax.grid(True)
1363        handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
1364        if handles:
1365            ncol = max(1, math.ceil(len(handles) / 12))
1366            ax.legend(
1367                title=INDEX_COL,
1368                fontsize="small",
1369                ncol=ncol,
1370                loc="upper left",
1371                bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1.0),
1372            )
1373        ax.set_title("Eigenvalue tracking")
1374        return ax

Scatter every run's eigenvalues, colored by eigenvalue index rather than by parameter value - a sanity check that track_eigenvalues() followed each mode correctly (a mode that jumps discontinuously between runs signals a tracking mistake).

Args: ax: axes to draw on (a new figure is created if omitted). xlim: "auto" (default) zooms the x-axis to the dominant eigenvalues (see EigenvalueSet.plot); pass an explicit (lo, hi) to override, or None for matplotlib's own full-range default. quantile: only used when xlim="auto" - see EigenvalueSet.plot. max_legend_entries: at most this many eigenvalues - the most dominant ones, by their largest (least negative) real part across the sweep - get a legend entry. With every eigenvalue of a large system otherwise labeled, the legend becomes an unreadable wall of entries; set to None to label all of them regardless.

class Sensitivity: 
1390class Sensitivity:
1391    """Change in every (tracked) eigenvalue's metrics between two modal
1392    analyses - build with `sensitivity_between`, which tracks the eigenvalues
1393    for you."""
1394
1395    def __init__(
1396        self,
1397        eig_before: EigenvalueSet,
1398        eig_after: EigenvalueSet,
1399        metrics: list[str] | None = None,
1400    ) -> None:
1401        if eig_before.get_indexes() != eig_after.get_indexes():
1402            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
1403                "Eigenvalue indexes must match to compute a sensitivity - "
1404                "track the eigenvalues first (see 'sensitivity_between'). "
1405                f"Got indexes {eig_before.get_indexes()} and {eig_after.get_indexes()}."
1406            )
1407        self.eig_before = eig_before
1408        self.eig_after = eig_after
1409        self.metrics = metrics or []
1410        self.df = eig_after - eig_before
1411        if self.metrics:
1412            self.df = self.df[self.metrics]
1413
1414    def filter_by_metrics(self, metrics: str | list[str]) -> Self:
1415        """Keep only the given eigenvalue metric column(s) (e.g. `"Damping ratio"`)."""
1416        metrics = [metrics] if isinstance(metrics, str) else list(metrics)
1417        return Sensitivity(self.eig_before, self.eig_after, metrics)
1418
1419    def filter_by_index(self, index: int | list[int]) -> Self:
1420        return self._filtered(
1421            self.eig_before.filter_by_index(index), self.eig_after.filter_by_index(index)
1422        )
1423
1424    def filter_by_damping_ratio(self, max_damping_ratio: float) -> Self:
1425        return self._filtered(
1426            self.eig_before.filter_by_damping_ratio(max_damping_ratio),
1427            self.eig_after.filter_by_damping_ratio(max_damping_ratio),
1428        )
1429
1430    def filter_out_conjugates(self) -> Self:
1431        return self._filtered(
1432            self.eig_before.filter_out_conjugates(), self.eig_after.filter_out_conjugates()
1433        )
1434
1435    def filter_out_real_modes(self) -> Self:
1436        return self._filtered(
1437            self.eig_before.filter_out_real_modes(), self.eig_after.filter_out_real_modes()
1438        )
1439
1440    def _filtered(self, eig_before: EigenvalueSet, eig_after: EigenvalueSet) -> Self:
1441        """Restrict both sides to the eigenvalue indexes that independently
1442        passed the filter on *both* sides - a mode can cross from real to
1443        complex (or vice versa) as the swept parameter changes, so filtering
1444        `eig_before` and `eig_after` separately can otherwise leave them with
1445        different indexes."""
1446        common = sorted(set(eig_before.get_indexes()) & set(eig_after.get_indexes()))
1447        return Sensitivity(
1448            eig_before.filter_by_index(common), eig_after.filter_by_index(common), self.metrics
1449        )
1450
1451    def get_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
1452        """`eigenvalue_after - eigenvalue_before` for every metric column,
1453        indexed by (tracked) eigenvalue index."""
1454        return self.df.copy()
1455
1456    def show(self) -> Styler:
1457        """Styled version of `get_dataframe()` - return it as the last
1458        expression of a notebook cell, or pass it to `display()`."""
1459        return (
1460            self.df.style.format(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION)
1461            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION, axis=0)
1462            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION, axis=1)
1463        )

def sensitivity_between( before: ModalAnalysisResults, after: ModalAnalysisResults) -> Sensitivity: 
1466def sensitivity_between(
1467    before: ModalAnalysisResults, after: ModalAnalysisResults
1468) -> Sensitivity:
1469    """Sensitivity of every eigenvalue's metrics between two modal analyses.
1470
1471    `after`'s eigenvalues are tracked against `before`'s first, so the
1472    subtraction lines up the same physical mode even if PowerFactory returned
1473    the eigenvalues in a different order.
1474    """
1475    tracked_after = after.track_eigenvalues_from(before)
1476    return Sensitivity(before.get_eigenvalues(), tracked_after.get_eigenvalues())

Sensitivity of every eigenvalue's metrics between two modal analyses.

after's eigenvalues are tracked against before's first, so the subtraction lines up the same physical mode even if PowerFactory returned the eigenvalues in a different order.

def system_matrix_sensitivity( before: ModalAnalysisResults, after: ModalAnalysisResults, delta: float) -> NDArray[numpy.complex128]: 
1479def system_matrix_sensitivity(
1480    before: ModalAnalysisResults, after: ModalAnalysisResults, delta: float
1481) -> npt.NDArray[np.complex128]:
1482    """Finite-difference estimate of `dA/dp`, the state matrix's sensitivity
1483    to a parameter `p`: `(after's state matrix - before's) / delta`, where
1484    `delta` is the change in `p` between the two runs.
1485
1486    Feed the result into `ModalAnalysisResults.eigenvalue_sensitivity` (on
1487    either `before` or `after` - the eigenvectors of both are valid
1488    evaluation points for a small enough `delta`) for the analytical,
1489    eigenvector-weighted eigenvalue sensitivity - see the module docstring
1490    and the *Dynamic Modal Analysis* tutorial for a comparison against
1491    `sensitivity_between`'s finite-difference-on-eigenvalues approach.
1492    """
1493    return (after.get_system_matrix() - before.get_system_matrix()) / delta

Finite-difference estimate of dA/dp, the state matrix's sensitivity to a parameter p: (after's state matrix - before's) / delta, where delta is the change in p between the two runs.

Feed the result into ModalAnalysisResults.eigenvalue_sensitivity (on either before or after - the eigenvectors of both are valid evaluation points for a small enough delta) for the analytical, eigenvector-weighted eigenvalue sensitivity - see the module docstring and the Dynamic Modal Analysis tutorial for a comparison against sensitivity_between's finite-difference-on-eigenvalues approach.

class ParametricSensitivity: 
1496class ParametricSensitivity:
1497    """Sensitivity across several conditions - e.g. the sensitivity of the
1498    eigenvalues to one parameter, recomputed at several values of a second
1499    ("condition") parameter. Build the list of `Sensitivity` objects yourself
1500    (one `sensitivity_between()` call per condition value - see the tutorial)
1501    and pass them in together with the condition values.
1502    """
1503
1504    def __init__(
1505        self,
1506        condition_values: Sequence[Any],
1507        sensitivities: Sequence[Sensitivity],
1508        normalization: Literal["column", "all"] | None = None,
1509    ) -> None:
1510        if len(condition_values) != len(sensitivities):
1511            raise PFEigenvalueMismatchError(
1512                "'condition_values' and 'sensitivities' must have the same "
1513                f"length; got {len(condition_values)} and {len(sensitivities)}."
1514            )
1515        self.condition_values = list(condition_values)
1516        self.sensitivities = list(sensitivities)
1517        self.normalization = normalization
1518        self.df = self._create_dataframe(
1519            self.condition_values, self.sensitivities
1520        )
1521
1522    def filter_by_metrics(self, metrics: str | list[str]) -> Self:
1523        sensitivities = [s.filter_by_metrics(metrics) for s in self.sensitivities]
1524        return ParametricSensitivity(
1525            self.condition_values, sensitivities, self.normalization
1526        )
1527
1528    def filter_by_index(self, index: int | list[int]) -> Self:
1529        sensitivities = [s.filter_by_index(index) for s in self.sensitivities]
1530        return ParametricSensitivity(
1531            self.condition_values, sensitivities, self.normalization
1532        )
1533
1534    def filter_by_damping_ratio(self, max_damping_ratio: float) -> Self:
1535        sensitivities = [
1536            s.filter_by_damping_ratio(max_damping_ratio) for s in self.sensitivities
1537        ]
1538        return ParametricSensitivity(
1539            self.condition_values, sensitivities, self.normalization
1540        )
1541
1542    def filter_out_conjugates(self) -> Self:
1543        sensitivities = [s.filter_out_conjugates() for s in self.sensitivities]
1544        return ParametricSensitivity(
1545            self.condition_values, sensitivities, self.normalization
1546        )
1547
1548    def filter_out_real_modes(self) -> Self:
1549        sensitivities = [s.filter_out_real_modes() for s in self.sensitivities]
1550        return ParametricSensitivity(
1551            self.condition_values, sensitivities, self.normalization
1552        )
1553
1554    def normalize(self, normalization: Literal["column", "all"]) -> Self:
1555        """Return a copy that `show()`s normalized (0-1) instead of raw values."""
1556        return ParametricSensitivity(
1557            self.condition_values, self.sensitivities, normalization
1558        )
1559
1560    def get_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
1561        return self.df.copy()
1562
1563    def show(self) -> Styler:
1564        """Styled version of `get_dataframe()` (with a colour gradient if
1565        `normalize()` was called) - return it as the last expression of a
1566        notebook cell, or pass it to `display()`."""
1567        df = self.df
1568        match self.normalization:
1569            case "column":
1570                styled = df.div(df.max(axis=1), axis=0).style.background_gradient(
1571                    axis=1, vmin=0, vmax=1, cmap="YlGnBu"
1572                )
1573            case "all":
1574                styled = df.div(df.max(axis=None), axis=0).style.background_gradient(
1575                    axis=None, vmin=0, vmax=1, cmap="YlGnBu"
1576                )
1577            case _:
1578                styled = df.style
1579        return (
1580            styled.format(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION)
1581            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION, axis=0)
1582            .format_index(precision=_STYLE_PRECISION, axis=1)
1583        )
1584
1585    def _create_dataframe(
1586        self, condition_values: list[Any], sensitivities: list[Sensitivity]
1587    ) -> DataFrame:
1588        df = pd.concat(
1589            [s.get_dataframe() for s in sensitivities], axis=1, keys=condition_values
1590        )
1591        return self._drop_unused_levels(df)
1592
1593    def _drop_unused_levels(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
1594        """Drop MultiIndex levels (rows or columns) that take only one value -
1595        no longer informative once e.g. every sensitivity has the same
1596        eigenvalue indexes."""
1597        result = df.copy()
1598        result.index = self._drop_unused_levels_of(df.index)
1599        result.columns = self._drop_unused_levels_of(df.columns)
1600        return result
1601
1602    def _drop_unused_levels_of(
1603        self, index: pd.MultiIndex | pd.Index
1604    ) -> pd.MultiIndex | pd.Index:
1605        if not isinstance(index, pd.MultiIndex):
1606            return index
1607        result = index
1608        for level in reversed(range(index.nlevels)):
1609            if result.nlevels > 1 and len(index.unique(level=level)) == 1:
1610                result = result.droplevel(level=level)
1611        return result
